Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in John-Michael L'Allier Create mediavine-create allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects Create: from n/a through 3.1.4.

KubeSphere 4.0.0 through 4.1.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the CertificateSigningRequest controller that allows attackers with permission to create CertificateSigningRequest objects to escalate privileges by exploiting automatic approval of requests carrying a kubesphere.io/username label without verifying the requester's identity or subject match. Attackers can submit a CertificateSigningRequest for the kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client signer with an arbitrary subject such as a platform administrator to obtain a cluster CA-signed client certificate, enabling authentication as the chosen identity and full cluster administrator privilege escalation.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.13, POST /api/integration/github/webhook in packages/plugins/integration-github/src/lib/probot/probot.discovery.ts passes request bodies through ProbotDiscovery.receiveHook to probot.receive without verifying x-hub-signature-256 against the configured webhook secret. Because the route is public and uses the attacker-controlled installation.id to locate integrations, an unauthenticated remote attacker who knows or guesses an installation identifier can forge installation deletion events that remove a tenant's GitHub integration or forge issues events that insert fabricated issue data into the tenant's automation pipeline. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.13.

A missing integrity verification vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow a low-privileged local attacker to modify trusted system data on the affected system.

A flaw was found in Submariner. In its default Pre-Shared Key (PSK) mode, all gateways within a broker set utilize the same PSK. An attacker, by knowing this shared PSK, can forge an Endpoint Custom Resource (CR) to impersonate another cluster's identity. This enables the attacker to establish an Internet Protocol Security (IPsec) tunnel under the false identity, leading to a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack on network traffic between clusters.

NetBird is a zero-trust networking platform that connects people, machines, and AI agents across any network. From versions 0.5.0 through 0.75.1, the client daemon exposes its gRPC control interface to any local process without authentication. On Linux, macOS, and FreeBSD, the interface is a Unix domain socket that is accessible to all local users, allowing any of them to control the daemon. An attacker with a low-privilege account can read or modify privileged VPN and daemon settings, disconnect or hijack the NetBird peer, and gain an unauthenticated root shell via the built-in SSH server. This issue is fixed in version 0.76.0.

A remote code execution vulnerability exists in the patch apply functionality of StellarProtect Linux and Stellar Agent (Linux) due to insufficient validation of uploaded patch packages before extraction. An attacker with low-privileged web access can upload a crafted patch package to execute arbitrary programs with root privileges on the server. This issue affects StellarProtect Linux: 1.0 and earlier; Stellar Agent (Linux): before 1.2.54. *Note: Stellar Agent (Linux) is the new name for StellarProtect Linux.
Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Arraytics WP Event Solution wp-event-solution allows Object Injection.This issue affects WP Event Solution: from n/a through 4.1.30.

Authentication bypass in the system.setPillar and system.getPillar functions in Uyuni before 5.1.35, 5.2.0 before 5.2.25, 5.3.0 before 5.3.5 could be used by logged in attackers to inject code into other managed system spaces.

SiYuan before 3.8.11 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject DOM event handlers by storing handler-named block attributes such as onmouseover. Attackers can share crafted .sy.zip packages or Markdown files whose attributes reach renderCustom or the unsanitised preview pane, executing OS commands via Node integration in the desktop app.

Traefik before 2.11.62, 3.x before 3.7.18, and 3.8.0-rc.1 contain an authentication bypass in the ForwardAuth middleware because connection isolation for NTLM and Negotiate credentials checks only the Authorization header, not Proxy-Authorization. Unauthenticated attackers can send such credentials in Proxy-Authorization to reuse a shared authentication-server connection already authenticated by another user, receive that user's identity via authResponseHeaders, and access backends as that user.

Traefik 3.7.15 before 3.7.18 and 3.8.0-rc.1 before 3.8.0-rc.2 contains a client certificate authentication bypass in the Kubernetes Ingress NGINX provider because, on hosts shared by multiple Ingresses using auth-tls-secret, Ssl-Client-* headers are built per Ingress while the TLS handshake uses the first Ingress's settings. Unauthenticated remote attackers can obtain Ssl-Client-Verify: SUCCESS with a client-chosen subject and issuer for an unverified certificate, or inject Ssl-Client-* headers directly, presenting forged identities to backends that trust the proxy.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows restricted subjects to execute arbitrary queries by calling the JavaScript surrealdb.query() bridge. Attackers permitted to run a specific script can bypass the Capabilities::allows_query() gate in the query module to execute unrestricted queries beyond their predefined operations.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authentication bypass in instance-level Google SSO because the id_token audience is not verified when no Google OAuth client ID is configured, the shipped default. Unauthenticated attackers can submit a Google-signed id_token minted for their own OAuth client to /api/sso/sign-in/common/google without an organizationId, obtaining a session as any existing user with the matching email.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains an authorization bypass in the internal database (TJDB) PostgREST proxy, which grants proxy access to every logged-in user and derives the database role and schema from the client-supplied tj-workspace-id header. Any authenticated workspace member can send requests to /api/tooljet-db/proxy/<tableId> to read and modify TJDB tables, bypassing app, query, and table permissions, and in SQL-mode-disabled (Cloud) deployments can access all tenants' tables.

Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in miniOrange miniorange otp verification miniorange-otp-verification allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects miniorange otp verification: from n/a through 5.6.2.

The Schema & Structured Data for WP & AMP plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in versions up to, and including, 1.68. This is due to deserialization of untrusted input via the admin export (saswp_export_all_settings_and_schema) which calls unrestricted unserialize() on every raw post meta value, combined with saswp_review_form_process_data() which stores unauthenticated-visitor-supplied reviewer-name data through update_post_meta — the plugin sanitizes with sanitize_text_field(), which does not recognise PHP serialization syntax or the NUL property-name delimiters, and WordPress's maybe_serialize/is_serialized has no case for the legacy PHP 'C' custom-serialization token (ArrayObject), so the payload is persisted byte-for-byte and never wrapped in a protective extra serialize layer. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject a PHP Object into the processing of the plugin. No known POP chain is present in the vulnerable plugin itself, but if a suitable chain exists via an additional plugin or theme installed on the blog, it could be used to delete arbitrary files, or achieve other impacts. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

D-Link DWM-222W developed by D-Link Corporation has a Use of Hard-coded Credentials vulnerability. Unauthenticated adjacent network attackers can use the administrator account embedded in the firmware to access the configuration backup endpoint and obtain plaintext passwords for all user accounts.

File Permission Vulnerability in RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware.

This issue affects RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware(CIM): before 98-09; RV3000 Log Monitor for VMware: before 97-05.

Missing authentication vulnerability in BS2500/BS500 Virtage Firmware.


This issue affects BladeSymphony BS2500: from 02-02 through 02-76; BladeSymphony BS500: from 01-01 through 02-76.

A vulnerability has been identified in Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 10 compatible) (All versions < V6.0.0), Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 11 compatible) (All versions < V6.0.0), Mendix OIDC Provider (Mendix 9 compatible) (All versions < V4.3.0). Affected versions of the module do not properly validate the integrity of JWTs submitted to the OIDC Provider Token Introspection endpoint, allowing tokens to be associated with legitimate token records based solely on their jti value.

This could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack an account (session) when gaining access to an jti of an active token.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in VideoWhisper.com Video Share VOD video-share-vod allows Path Traversal.This issue affects Video Share VOD: from n/a through 3.15.1.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Nickboss WordPress File Upload wp-file-upload allows Path Traversal.This issue affects WordPress File Upload: from n/a through 5.3.1.
Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 2.0.0.
Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type vulnerability in theMarketer theMarketer themarketer allows Using Malicious Files.This issue affects theMarketer: from n/a through 1.5.9.

Pydantic Deep 0.2.18 before 0.4.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the bundled DeepResearch FastAPI app that exposes HTTP routes and the /ws/chat WebSocket. Remote attackers reaching the server bound to all interfaces can enumerate sessions, read event logs and workspace files, drive the research agent, and delete sessions.
In Apache Airflow < 1.10.12, the "origin" parameter passed to some of the endpoints like '/trigger' was vulnerable to XSS exploit.
In Apache Airflow, prior to version 2.4.1, deactivating a user wouldn't prevent an already authenticated user from being able to continue using the UI or API.

A flaw was found in Quarkus where HTTP security policies are not sanitizing certain character permutations correctly when accepting requests, resulting in incorrect evaluation of permissions. This issue could allow an attacker to bypass the security policy altogether, resulting in unauthorized endpoint access and possibly a denial of service.

An improper input validation flaw was found in the eBPF subsystem in the Linux kernel. The issue occurs due to a lack of proper validation of dynamic pointers within user-supplied eBPF programs prior to executing them. This may allow an attacker with CAP_BPF privileges to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of the kernel.

A flaw was found in Keycloak, where it does not properly validate URLs included in a redirect. This issue could allow an attacker to construct a malicious request to bypass validation and access other URLs and sensitive information within the domain or conduct further attacks. This flaw affects any client that utilizes a wildcard in the Valid Redirect URIs field, and requires user interaction within the malicious URL.

A flaw was found in the github.com/containers/image library. This flaw allows attackers to trigger unexpected authenticated registry accesses on behalf of a victim user, causing resource exhaustion, local path traversal, and other attacks.

A flaw was found in cri-o. A malicious container can create a symbolic link to arbitrary files on the host via directory traversal (“../“). This flaw allows the container to read and write to arbitrary files on the host system.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. Certain endpoints in Keycloak's admin REST API allow low-privilege users to access administrative functionalities. This flaw allows users to perform actions reserved for administrators, potentially leading to data breaches or system compromise.

A flaw was found in openshift-gitops-operator-container. The openshift.io/cluster-monitoring label is applied to all namespaces that deploy an ArgoCD CR instance, allowing the namespace to create a rogue PrometheusRule. This issue can have adverse effects on the platform monitoring stack, as the rule is rolled out cluster-wide when the label is applied.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Shinetheme Traveler traveler.This issue affects Traveler: from n/a before 3.2.1.
A flaw was found in Podman. The podman machine init command fails to verify the TLS certificate when downloading the VM images from an OCI registry. This issue results in a Man In The Middle attack.

There's a vulnerability in podman where an attacker may use the kube play command to overwrite host files when the kube file container a Secrete or a ConfigMap volume mount and such volume contains a symbolic link to a host file path. In a successful attack, the attacker can only control the target file to be overwritten but not the content to be written into the file.

Binary-Affected: podman
Upstream-version-introduced: v4.0.0
Upstream-version-fixed: v5.6.1

A flaw was found in Hibernate. A remote attacker with low privileges could exploit a second-order SQL injection vulnerability by providing specially crafted, unsanitized non-alphanumeric characters in the ID column when the InlineIdsOrClauseBuilder is used. This could lead to sensitive information disclosure, such as reading system files, and allow for data manipulation or deletion within the application's database, resulting in an application level denial of service.

A flaw was found in rubyipmi, a gem used in the Baseboard Management Controller (BMC) component of Red Hat Satellite. An authenticated attacker with host creation or update permissions could exploit this vulnerability by crafting a malicious username for the BMC interface. This could lead to remote code execution (RCE) on the system.

A flaw was found in Foreman. A remote attacker could exploit a command injection vulnerability in Foreman's WebSocket proxy implementation. This vulnerability arises from the system's use of unsanitized hostname values from compute resource providers when constructing shell commands. By operating a malicious compute resource server, an attacker could achieve remote code execution on the Foreman server when a user accesses VM VNC console functionality. This could lead to the compromise of sensitive credentials and the entire managed infrastructure.

A flaw was found in Corosync. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit a wrong return value vulnerability in the Corosync membership commit token sanity check by sending a specially crafted User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet. This can lead to an out-of-bounds read, causing a denial of service (DoS) and potentially disclosing limited memory contents
Crucial management API endpoints for cellular eSIM allocation do not validate caller authorization, allowing remote profiles to be rewritten or deleted.
System log files output unencrypted SMTP server authentication passwords alongside sensitive employee corporate identification data.

A flaw was found in Netty. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit a vulnerability in Netty's HTTP/1 to HTTP/2 conversion process. When an HTTP/1 request includes both an absolute-form request-target and a conflicting Host header, Netty incorrectly prioritizes the Host header for the HTTP/2 :authority field, discarding the original request-target authority. This inconsistency can allow an attacker to bypass security controls in Netty-based proxies or gateways, potentially leading to unauthorized access, cache poisoning, or misrouting of requests.

U-Boot versions 2025.07 before 2026.10-rc5 contain a use-after-free vulnerability in the httpc_recv_cb() function within the lwIP wget implementation. When HTTP data storage fails, the callback frees the connection PCB but returns ERR_BUF instead of ERR_ABRT, causing the TCP input path to access released memory and crash the bootloader.

A flaw was found in Foreman. A command injection vulnerability exists in the foreman-rake errors:fetch_log task. The request_id parameter is passed to an underlying system command (typically grep) without adequate shell neutralization. While the task is intended to fetch specific log entries, an attacker with sudo permissions to execute this rake task can inject shell metacharacters (such as ;, ", or |) to break out of the intended command and execute arbitrary code.

A flaw was found in Foreman. OS command injection vulnerabilities exist in the foreman-rake db:dump and db:import_dump tasks. The application fails to properly sanitize user-supplied input in the destination parameter (during backups) and the file parameter (during imports) before passing them to a Ruby system() call for execution. An attacker with permissions to execute foreman-rake (e.g., via a restricted sudo configuration) can append malicious shell commands to the provided file paths.

A flaw was found in gst-plugins-base. A heap buffer overflow can be triggered when processing video buffers whose attached GstVideoMeta metadata declares plane strides and offsets that exceed the actual backing memory allocation. The metadata is not range-checked during deserialization, and the video frame mapping code does not verify that the declared plane geometry fits within the buffer before allowing consumers to read or write video data. A local attacker who controls the sending side of a GStreamer inter-process IPC pipeline can deliver a crafted buffer carrying fabricated strides, causing the receiving process to read or write beyond heap boundaries. Successful exploitation can cause a denial of service or potentially allow code execution within the affected process.

Fluxion before 6.39 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the fluxion.sh target scanner, which decodes access point ESSIDs with eval after escaping only single quotes. Attackers within Wi-Fi range can broadcast an access point with a crafted SSID to execute commands as root when the operator scans or selects it.

A flaw was found in dnf5daemon-server. Unauthenticated D-Bus methods pass caller-controlled URL or .rpm path patterns into a root-privileged cmdline package loader that may store fetched content in a world-readable cache without size limits, or open local paths as root, allowing a local attacker to disclose privileged content and to deny service via disk exhaustion.

Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure Managed Instance for Apache Cassandra allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over an adjacent network.

SRS 4.0.0 before 6.0.194, 7.0.0 before 7.0.214, and 8.0.0 before 8.0.73 contains a heap-based buffer overflow in SrsRtcpCommon::decode and SrsRtcpTWCC::decode that lets remote WebRTC peers write past the fixed 1500-byte payload_ array. Unauthenticated attackers opening a WHIP or WHEP session can send oversized BYE, APP, unknown-type or TWCC RTCP packets to overwrite up to 64 KB of heap memory, crashing the server.

OpenProject 17.2.0 before 17.5.2, 17.6.0 before 17.6.1, 17.7.0 before 17.7.3, 17.8.0 before 17.8.2, and 17.9.0 before 17.9.7 contains an externally controlled method selection vulnerability in InplaceEditFieldsController via the unvalidated attribute parameter. Users who can view a project can request the inplace_edit_fields reset route with attribute destroy to delete projects and subprojects, or invoke other methods exposing restricted data.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability. An attacker with local access to the appliance could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information, modification of protected resources, and execution of privileged operations within the appliance security context, potentially resulting in compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability. An attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive information, unauthorized modification of system resources, and execution of privileged actions that could lead to compromise of the appliance.

Denial of Service in DefaultPluginManager in Apache JSPWIKI versions prior to the fixed version on all platforms allows an attacker to spawn multiple threads until resource exhaustion or to class load any class on the classpath and creating an instance of it.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability. An attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to system resources, disclosure of sensitive information, modification of protected configurations, and execution of privileged operations.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability. A local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive data, modification of critical resources, and disruption of appliance functionality.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Missing Authentication for Critical Function vulnerability. An attacker with local access to the appliance could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information, unauthorized modification of application data, and execution of actions with elevated privileges within the appliance environment.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Out-of-bounds Write vulnerability. A local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to application instability, denial of service, disclosure of sensitive information, arbitrary memory modification, and potentially execution of attacker-controlled code within the affected process.

Incorrect permission assignment for critical resource in the media management functionality of Progress Software Sitefinity versions before 14.4.8154, from 15.0.8200 before 15.0.8236, from 15.1.8300 before 15.1.8337, from 15.2.8400 before 15.2.8444, from 15.3.8500 before 15.3.8533, and from 15.4.8600 before 15.4.8642 allows unauthorized modification of media library content under certain configurations.

HortusFox (hortusfox-web) through 6.4 contains a password reset poisoning vulnerability in UserModel::restorePassword that builds reset links from the client-controlled Host header. Unauthenticated attackers can request a reset with a forged Host header to capture the victim's reset token and take over accounts including administrators.

A data-query neutralization weakness in the query builder of the MongoDB integration for a PHP web framework allows values supplied to certain bulk counter-update helpers to be interpreted by the database as query expressions rather than stored as plain text. An application that passes externally supplied data into these helpers may write unintended values into stored documents and may result in unintended disclosure of other data held on the same document. No credentials are required of the party supplying the value.

An improper restriction of dynamically determined object attributes in the object-document mapping library's association handling allows structured input supplied in place of a simple identifier value to be turned into an object that is treated as an already-stored record of a caller-chosen model class. In applications that pass unfiltered request data into the affected association handling, an unauthenticated party may cause unintended modification or removal of stored records, and may render an individual record unreadable through that association.

An out-of-bounds read in the native C BSON decoding extension of the MongoDB Python Driver may allow an unauthenticated party who can supply crafted BSON data to the decoder to cause the application process to terminate. In some configurations, nearby process memory may be included in error messages, which may result in limited unintended disclosure of data.

Camunda 8.8.0 before 8.8.47, 8.9.0 before 8.9.29, 8.10.0 before 8.10.10, and 8.11.0-alpha1 contain an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the persistent web session feature, which stores session attributes as Java-serialized data in secondary storage and deserializes them via an ObjectInputStream without an ObjectInputFilter. Attackers with write access to the web session index, such as an unauthenticated Elasticsearch cluster deployed via Camunda's docker-compose files, can plant a crafted serialized object and trigger deserialization by presenting a matching session cookie, which combined with a gadget chain like the bundled Commons Collections 3.1-RC1 library can lead to code execution as the Camunda service account.

VMware ESX contains a stack-based buffer-overflow vulnerability in the VMkernel. Broadcom has evaluated the severity of this issue to be in the Important severity range with a maximum CVSSv3 base score of 8.2.
Affected versions:
VMware ESX 9.1.x.x: fixed in ESXi-9.1.2.0-25946735

VMware Telco Cloud Platform 5.0.x: fixed in KB463501
VMware Telco Cloud Platform 5.1.x: fixed in KB463501

A maliciously modified field in the locally stored JSON description for an update made available by Autodesk, when processed by Autodesk Access, can cause attacker-controlled HTML content to be executed in another user's session. A local, authenticated malicious actor can leverage this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of another user if that user interacts with an injected link, resulting in privilege escalation.

FreeRDP before 3.33.0 contains an integer overflow in the client GDI handling of accumulated drawing-order bounds: wrapped INT32 coordinates yield a zero-width clip region that causes clipping to be skipped in gdi_FillRect. A malicious RDP server can send many ORDER_BOUNDS orders followed by an OPAQUE_RECT order to trigger a heap out-of-bounds write past the client's drawing bitmap, potentially leading to code execution.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability where WebDAV sync error formatting skips HTML escaping for certain malformed-response errors, passing raw markup to the Electron notification renderer. A network attacker who alters a cleartext HTTP WebDAV response can inject event-handler markup that, when the victim manually starts sync, executes JavaScript with Node integration as the logged-in user.

Missing authentication vulnerability in BS2500/BS500 Virtage Firmware.

This issue affects BladeSymphony BS2500: from 02-02 through 02-76*; BladeSymphony BS500: from 01-01 through 02-76*.

A flaw was found in Flatpak’s flatpak-system-helper. When a system-wide app, runtime, or extension uses the extra-data mechanism and its apply_extra logic creates a deeply nested directory tree, permission canonicalization can fail (for example with EMFILE). Affected Flatpak versions can still report success without clearing setuid/setgid bits, leaving a setuid-root executable under /var/lib/flatpak. A local attacker who can install or update such content system-wide, or who can already execute code as a local user in cooperation with that content, can escalate privileges to root.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Download of Code Without Integrity Check vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.
Various logic errors in view processing can cause incorrect cached results to be returned.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Script injection.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Heap-based Buffer Overflow vulnerability. An unauthenticated local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Cache poisoning and Denial of service.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2 contains a path traversal vulnerability in integration nodes that build API request paths from unencoded record, table, or resource ID parameters. Attackers can supply relative path segments through untrusted input such as webhook bodies to read, modify, or delete unintended resources using the node's stored credential.

n8n before 1.123.96, 2.x before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 does not verify that the user activating a workflow can access the credentials set on its trigger nodes. An authenticated member who knows another user's credential ID can activate a workflow whose trigger uses it, causing n8n to create or delete webhooks on the connected service with that credential's privileges and deliver events from attacker-chosen resources to the member's workflow.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Hive Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to execute arbtrary commands in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Hive Provider versions prior to 4.1.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case HIve Provider is installed (Hive Provider 4.1.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the HIve Provider version 4.1.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version that has lower version of the Hive Provider installed).

The reference count changes made as part of the CVE-2023-33951 and CVE-2023-33952 fixes exposed a use-after-free flaw in the way memory objects were handled when they were being used to store a surface. When running inside a VMware guest with 3D acceleration enabled, a local, unprivileged user could potentially use this flaw to escalate their privileges.

A vulnerability was found in Perl. This security issue occurs while Perl for Windows relies on the system path environment variable to find the shell (`cmd.exe`). When running an executable that uses the Windows Perl interpreter, Perl attempts to find and execute `cmd.exe` within the operating system. However, due to path search order issues, Perl initially looks for cmd.exe in the current working directory. This flaw allows an attacker with limited privileges to place`cmd.exe` in locations with weak permissions, such as `C:\ProgramData`. By doing so, arbitrary code can be executed when an administrator attempts to use this executable from these compromised locations.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the netfilter subsystem of the Linux kernel. If the catchall element is garbage-collected when the pipapo set is removed, the element can be deactivated twice. This can cause a use-after-free issue on an NFT_CHAIN object or NFT_OBJECT object, allowing a local unprivileged user with CAP_NET_ADMIN capability to escalate their privileges on the system.

A use-after-free flaw was found in the Linux Kernel. When a disk is removed, bdi_unregister is called to stop further write-back and waits for associated delayed work to complete. However, wb_inode_writeback_end() may schedule bandwidth estimation work after this has completed, which can result in the timer attempting to access the recently freed bdi_writeback.

A vulnerability was found in Undertow. This vulnerability impacts a server that supports the wildfly-http-client protocol. Whenever a malicious user opens and closes a connection with the HTTP port of the server and then closes the connection immediately, the server will end with both memory and open file limits exhausted at some point, depending on the amount of memory available. 

At HTTP upgrade to remoting, the WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit leaks connections if RemotingConnection is closed by Remoting ServerConnectionOpenListener. Because the remoting connection originates in Undertow as part of the HTTP upgrade, there is an external layer to the remoting connection. This connection is unaware of the outermost layer when closing the connection during the connection opening procedure. Hence, the Undertow WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit is not notified of the closed connection in this scenario. Because WriteTimeoutStreamSinkConduit creates a timeout task, the whole dependency tree leaks via that task, which is added to XNIO WorkerThread. So, the workerThread points to the Undertow conduit, which contains the connections and causes the leak.

A flaw was found in the QEMU disk image utility (qemu-img) 'info' command. A specially crafted image file containing a `json:{}` value describing block devices in QMP could cause the qemu-img process on the host to consume large amounts of memory or CPU time, leading to denial of service or read/write to an existing external file.

A vulnerability was found in Undertow, where the chunked response hangs after the body was flushed. The response headers and body were sent but the client would continue waiting as Undertow does not send the expected 0\r\n termination of the chunked response. This results in uncontrolled resource consumption, leaving the server side to a denial of service attack. This happens only with Java 17 TLSv1.3 scenarios.

A vulnerability was found in Buildah. Cache mounts do not properly validate that user-specified paths for the cache are within our cache directory, allowing a `RUN` instruction in a Container file to mount an arbitrary directory from the host (read/write) into the container as long as those files can be accessed by the user running Buildah.

A script injection vulnerability was identified in the Tuned package. The `instance_create()` D-Bus function can be called by locally logged-in users without authentication. This flaw allows a local non-privileged user to execute a D-Bus call with `script_pre` or `script_post` options that permit arbitrary scripts with their absolute paths to be passed. These user or attacker-controlled executable scripts or programs could then be executed by Tuned with root privileges that could allow attackers to local privilege escalation.

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

i3c: dw: Fix use-after-free in dw_i3c_master driver due to race condition

In dw_i3c_common_probe, &master->hj_work is bound with
dw_i3c_hj_work. And dw_i3c_master_irq_handler can call
dw_i3c_master_irq_handle_ibis function to start the work.

If we remove the module which will call dw_i3c_common_remove to
make cleanup, it will free master->base through i3c_master_unregister
while the work mentioned above will be used. The sequence of operations
that may lead to a UAF bug is as follows:

CPU0                                      CPU1

                                     | dw_i3c_hj_work
dw_i3c_common_remove                 |
i3c_master_unregister(&master->base) |
device_unregister(&master->dev)      |
device_release                       |
//free master->base                  |
                                     | i3c_master_do_daa(&master->base)
                                     | //use master->base

Fix it by ensuring that the work is canceled before proceeding with
the cleanup in dw_i3c_common_remove.

A flaw was found in the RandR extension, where the RRChangeProviderProperty function does not properly validate input. This issue leads to an integer overflow when computing the total size to allocate.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Satellite (Foreman component). This vulnerability allows an authenticated user with edit_settings permissions to achieve arbitrary command execution on the underlying operating system via insufficient server-side validation of command whitelisting.

A flaw was found in fog-kubevirt. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack due to disabled certificate validation. This enables the attacker to intercept and potentially alter sensitive communications between Satellite and OpenShift, resulting in information disclosure and data integrity compromise.

A flaw was found in foreman_kubevirt. When configuring the connection to OpenShift, the system disables SSL verification if a Certificate Authority (CA) certificate is not explicitly set. This insecure default allows a remote attacker, capable of intercepting network traffic between Satellite and OpenShift, to perform a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack. Such an attack could lead to the disclosure or alteration of sensitive information.

A flaw was found in Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) llama-stack-operator. This vulnerability allows unauthorized access to Llama Stack services deployed in other namespaces via direct network requests, because no NetworkPolicy restricts access to the llama-stack service endpoint. As a result, a user in one namespace can access another user’s Llama Stack instance and potentially view or manipulate sensitive data.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated user with the uma_protection role can bypass User-Managed Access (UMA) policy validation. This allows the attacker to include resource identifiers owned by other users in a policy creation request, even if the URL path specifies an attacker-owned resource. Consequently, the attacker gains unauthorized permissions to victim-owned resources, enabling them to obtain a Requesting Party Token (RPT) and access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions.

BusyBox versions 1.27.0 before 1.38.0, fixed in commit 42202bf, contain a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in the DHCPv6 client (udhcpc6) DNS_SERVERS option handler in networking/udhcp/d6_dhcpc.c that allows network-adjacent attackers to trigger memory corruption by sending a crafted DHCPv6 response with a malformed D6_OPT_DNS_SERVERS option. Attackers can exploit incorrect heap buffer allocation calculations in the option_to_env() function to cause denial of service or achieve arbitrary code execution on embedded systems without heap hardening.

A flaw was found in Samba’s certificate auto-enrollment Group Policy handling. When certificate auto-enrollment is enabled, Samba may retrieve a CA certificate over an unencrypted HTTP connection and install it into the local trust store without proper verification. An attacker with the ability to intercept or redirect network traffic could exploit this behavior to supply a malicious certificate authority certificate, potentially allowing interception or spoofing of trusted communications.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. The ansible-galaxy role install command processes dependency specifications from a role's meta/requirements.yml file. Due to improper neutralization of argument delimiters, a malicious role author can inject arbitrary git configuration flags through the src field. This allows arbitrary code execution on the machine of a user who installs the role via ansible-galaxy role install.

A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland. A mismatch between the X server and the libXfont2 library's maximum font name length can cause a stack buffer overflow during font alias resolution. The server allocates a 256 byte stack buffer but libXfont2's alias target name length is 1024 bytes. A font alias name between 257 and 1023 bytes causes the X server to copy that name into the undersized stack buffer without further checks. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland. The X server has multiple stack buffers sized XkbMaxShiftLevel * XkbNumKbdGroups but CheckKeyTypes() does not verify or clamp non-canonical key types to XkbMaxShiftLevel. A client can change key types to excessive shift levels and trigger stack overflows. This is caused by an incomplete fix of CVE-2025-26597. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

A stack-based buffer overflow flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland. _XkbSetMapChecks() declares a fixed-size stack buffer mapWidths[256] indexed by key type index. The helper function CheckKeyTypes() writes to this buffer at a client-controlled offset, allowing a stack buffer overflow. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

An out-of-bounds write flaw was found in the X.Org X server and Xwayland in DRIGetBuffers/DRIGetBuffersWithFormat. A client that requests multiple DRI2BufferBackLeft attachments and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft can trigger an out-of-bounds heap write. This may be used to crash the server, or for privilege escalation if the X server runs as root.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. The fix for a previous vulnerability (CVE-2022-4318) was incorrect, allowing it to be bypassed. An attacker capable of setting environment variables on a container can inject a newline character into the HOME environment variable. This issue allows the addition of arbitrary lines into /etc/passwd by use of a specially crafted environment variable.

A flaw was found in ansible-core. The _extract_collection_from_git() function in ansible-core's concrete_artifact_manager.py constructs git clone commands without a '--' (end-of-options) separator before user-supplied URLs when installing collections from git sources. An attacker who provides a crafted collection source URI containing git argument injection payloads can achieve arbitrary command execution when a user runs 'ansible-galaxy collection install' with the malicious source. This is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-11332, which hardened the role install path but missed the equivalent collection install code path.

A flaw was found in Picketlink's SP signature validation; a SAML response containing zero assertion elements matching the signature check can allow an attacker to forge a SAML response and auth as any principal with any roles on the protected application.

A flaw was found in rpm. An attacker can exploit a command injection vulnerability by influencing the path or filename of a tarball processed by `rpmbuild -t*` to include shell metacharacters. This is particularly relevant in automated build or continuous integration (CI) workflows that ingest externally supplied artifact names. Successful exploitation allows for arbitrary command execution with the privileges of the build user, which could lead to information disclosure or disruption of the build environment.

Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic in the GridFS component of the MongoDB Go Driver can cause a caller-supplied structured file identifier to be interpreted as a query condition rather than as a literal identifier. An authenticated user who can influence the identifier passed by an affected application may cause all GridFS file chunks in the affected bucket to be removed, rendering stored file content unreadable.

A flaw was found in rpm. An attacker can supply a crafted manifest file that, when processed by a user or automation using `rpm -q -p` or similar manifest-processing flows, leads to arbitrary code execution. This occurs because manifest entries are unexpectedly macro-expanded before being opened, allowing embedded shell commands to run with the privileges of the `rpm` process. Successful exploitation can lead to a full compromise of confidentiality, integrity, and availability for the affected account.

A command injection flaw was found in rpm. Installing or rebuilding a source RPM whose source or spec file basenames contain a %() macro construct causes rpm to execute an attacker-controlled shell command via popen() while relocating the source file list. This allows arbitrary command execution as the invoking (typically non-root) user, simply by installing, rebuilding, or otherwise processing an untrusted .src.rpm.

A flaw was found in cifs-utils. This flaw allows an unprivileged local user to achieve privilege escalation. When a privileged service mounts a Common Internet File System (CIFS) share using a user-controlled credentials file, input values are not properly sanitized before being assembled into mount options. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability to inject unauthorized mount options, allowing them to bypass permission checks and execute files with administrative (root) privileges.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in libavcodec/lcevcdec.c because LCEVC output picture dimensions are not validated against the allocated frame. Attackers can embed crafted LCEVC enhancement data with differing global configurations in H.264 or HEVC streams to corrupt heap memory in decoding applications.

A flaw was found in the interaction between systemd-gpt-auto-generator and 
confidential computing guest VM images in OpenShift Sandboxed Containers 
(confidential peer pods). systemd-gpt-auto-generator automatically discovers 
and mounts GPT partitions by type GUID at boot with no user confirmation. In 
the confidential computing threat model, where the host/hypervisor is the 
adversary, a malicious host can inject partitions into the guest's virtual 
disk. Most critically, injecting a swap partition causes the guest kernel to 
page out TEE-encrypted memory to a host-controlled block device, breaking the 
confidentiality guarantee of the hardware TEE (AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX).

The PodVM images use a GPT-partitioned disk with dm-verity on the root 
partition. However, the roothash= kernel parameter only disables root 
auto-discovery — non-root partitions (swap, /home, /var, /srv, /var/tmp) are 
still auto-discovered and mounted. The generator is shipped unmasked in the 
RHEL systemd-udev subpackage, and no kernel command line parameter in the 
measured UKI addon disables it. Additionally, the PodVM measurement script 
captures PCRs 3, 9, 11, and 12, but not PCR 5 (GPT partition table), so 
partition table modifications are not detected by remote attestation.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge privileged actions such as administrator user creation by merging $_GET and $_POST parameters without requiring an anti-CSRF token. Attackers can craft a malicious link or auto-navigating page that issues a plain GET request, exploiting the lack of CSRF protection and SameSite=Lax cookie behavior on top-level navigations to create unauthorized administrator accounts.

A path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) was found in ansible-core's ansible-galaxy role installation. An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. A name containing "../" escapes that directory, and an absolute name replaces it entirely. Because ansible-galaxy processes transitive dependencies from an installed role's meta/requirements.yml, a malicious role publisher can cause attacker-supplied files to be written outside the operator's chosen roles directory when the operator installs the role, and, when --force is used, can cause an existing role directory outside that path to be removed and replaced. The impact is bounded by the invoking user's filesystem permissions and requires the operator to install the attacker-influenced content.

WLA DX 9.7 before 10.8 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in parse_data_blocks() in wlalink/analyze.c that copies section namespaces without length checks. Attackers can supply a crafted object or library file with a namespace longer than 255 bytes or unterminated to overflow the 256-byte stack buffer when linked.

A flaw was found in hypershift-addon. Due to an overly permissive role-based access control (RBAC) configuration that grants permissions to all authenticated users rather than restricting them to the addon service, a low-privileged authenticated user can view, modify, or delete managed cluster resources. This improper authorization allows unauthorized users to alter or disrupt clusters across the entire managed fleet.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 missing authorization allowed any authenticated user to start and stop cloud agent instances
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 missing authorization allowed project viewers to remove VCS roots
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2, 2026.1.4, 2025.11.8 project viewers could redirect GitHub App connection credentials of parent projects

A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

cves.description: diffpy.structure before 3.5.1 contains a code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run Python code by supplying crafted CIF symmetry operations passed to eval() in get_symop(). Attackers can embed expressions in the _space_group_symop_operation_xyz or _symmetry_equiv_pos_as_xyz loop to execute code with victim privileges when the CIF file is parsed locally.

audio-separator before 0.47.2 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying malicious Demucs .th model files loaded via torch.load with weights_only=False. Local users writing to the shared /tmp/audio-separator-models/ default directory, or attackers controlling unverified model download sources, can execute code when victims run Demucs separation.

The Tutor LMS – eLearning and online course solution plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.0 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to permanently delete any comment they authored anywhere on the site — including regular post comments and lesson comments — along with all replies to those comments authored by any other user, including Administrators and Instructors.

Grav Form plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Form::uploadFiles(), which sanitizes SVG only when a file's last extension is .svg and accepts markup under unrecognized extensions. Anonymous attackers can upload files like drawing.svg.foo through public any-type upload forms, running script in an administrator's session when opened, enabling super-admin creation on Grav 2.x with Admin2.

Dockhand before 1.0.57 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows non-admin users with settings:edit permission to modify OIDC provider configuration due to an improper permission check. Attackers can send a PUT request to /api/auth/oidc/<provider-id> setting adminClaim to their own OIDC group, gaining full admin access on their next OIDC login.

When Request::getBaseUrl() does not find the script name at the start of the request URI, it looks for it further into the path. This supports web servers that rewrite every URL to a front controller in a subdirectory. The base URL then kept everything before the script name, and the client chooses that part. A request URI starting with // or /\ made the base URL start with a host.

With SCRIPT_NAME=/public/index.php, a request for //evil.example/public/index.php/login is routed to /login, with the base URL //evil.example/public/index.php and the base path //evil.example/public. The URLs generated for that page then point to evil.example:
- links built with path() and the actions of forms, so a login form sends the credentials of the user to evil.example;
- redirects to generated URLs, such as the ones of redirectToRoute();
- assets referenced with a relative path through asset(), so the page can load scripts from evil.example.

The attacker has to make a user follow a crafted link, such as https://app.example//evil.example/public/index.php/login. framework.trusted_hosts does not help, since the host of the request is the real one.

Applications are affected when their front controller is in a subdirectory and the web server sends it URIs that do not start with that directory. A .htaccess file at the root of the project that rewrites every URL to public/ does that, for instance.

Applications are also affected when the web server sets SCRIPT_NAME to the path of the request. Some nginx configurations do that when they send every request to the front controller without fastcgi_split_path_info. php -S does it too, with a router script outside the document root. A request for /\evil.example/index.php then gets the base URL /\evil.example/index.php, which browsers read as a link to evil.example.

The configurations recommended in the Symfony documentation are not affected.

Request::getBaseUrl() now returns an empty base URL when the request URI starts with // or /\.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the computing unit workflow websocket of Apache Texera (incubating) allows an authenticated user to view workflow results, control workflow executions, and run code in a computing unit they have not been granted. In local JVM and single-node Docker Compose deployments this is possible directly; in Kubernetes deployments it is possible from code running inside another computing unit in the cluster.



This issue affects Apache Texera : from 1.1.0 through 1.2.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0, which fixes the issue. Local JVM and Docker Compose deployments do not provide the full security model and should only be used by trusted users.

HortusFox is a self-hosted web application for collaborative plant management. Prior to 6.2, the toggle_boolean_value() handler in app/controller/admin.php passes the name parameter of the /admin/environment/boolean/toggle route in app/config/routes.php to AppModel::updateSingle() in app/models/AppModel.php, which concatenates the parameter into the SQL UPDATE identifier position without validation. An unauthenticated attacker can induce a signed-in administrator to open a crafted link, causing SQL injection that permits expressions and subqueries to read database contents, including an administrator password hash, or modify settings to enable passwordless administrator access. The hash alone does not permit direct login. This issue is fixed in version 6.2.

Genetec Security Center can expose access control unit credentials in plain text in server log files when specific non-default logging options are enabled. An attacker with local access to the affected log files could retrieve and use these credentials.

A flaw was found in the file-psd plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PSD (Photoshop Document) image file in LAB color mode, the plugin does not properly validate that a fourth channel is present when the transparency flag is set. This mismatch causes the merged-image path to allocate buffers for three components while performing color conversion with four-component formats, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

Nektos act 0.2.92 before 0.2.95 contains an argument injection vulnerability in readProjectArgsFile and projectFlag that allows malicious repositories to bypass the untrusted project .actrc flag allowlist. Attackers can commit a crafted .actrc smuggling disallowed flags like -P self-hosted or --privileged to run workflow steps on the developer's host.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an insecure default configuration in its Windows setup.bat script that provisions an administrator account with the credentials admin/admin and SSL disabled. Unauthenticated network attackers can log in over plain HTTP on port 10000 with these unchanged credentials to gain full Webmin administrative access.

FCEUX before 2.8.0 contains an integer overflow in SetBoardName() in src/unif.cpp that allows crafted UNIF ROM files to write past a heap buffer. Attackers can persuade users to open a .unf file with a 0xFFFFFFFF MAPR chunk length, wrapping the allocation to zero and corrupting heap memory to crash the emulator or execute code.

FCEUX 2.5.0 before 2.8.0 contains an integer overflow in iNESLoad() in src/ines.cpp that allows a crafted NES 2.0 ROM to write past a heap buffer. Attackers can persuade users to open a .nes file using exponent-multiplier PRG ROM size notation with mappers 53, 198, 228 or 547 to corrupt memory, crashing the emulator and possibly executing code.

OneDev before 17.2.4 contains an argument injection vulnerability in commit query handling that allows authenticated attackers to inject git options through branch or tag names. Attackers can push a branch named like --output=<path> and query it via the commits page or REST API to overwrite server-writable files, causing denial of service.

PyBioNetGen 0.8.7 contains a code injection vulnerability in ParameterBlock.add_item() and ModelBlock.add_item() that allows attackers to execute Python code by passing parameter expressions to sympy.sympify(). Attackers can supply a crafted BNG-XML model file with Python code in a Parameter expr or value attribute to execute code as the user when loaded with bionetgen.bngmodel().

asar-py before 0.1.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in AsarArchive.extract() and extract_archive() that allows attackers to write files outside the destination directory via crafted archive headers. Attackers can supply a .asar archive with '..' path components or malicious symlink targets to write files such as usercustomize.py, leading to code execution.

openIMIS before 2026-10 contains a broken access control vulnerability in the FHIR R4 module that allows any authenticated attacker to delete Coverage policy records due to an empty permissions_delete list being vacuously granted by user.has_perms([]). Attackers can issue a DELETE request to the Coverage/<uuid>/ endpoint to permanently and irrecoverably remove insurance policy records.

C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to open a malicious project file delivered through common distribution channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media.

An invalid memory release in the MongoDB PHP Driver extension occurs when certain string-typed options or type-mapping settings are given non-string values. A party who can run PHP code in a process that loads the extension may corrupt process memory. This can lead to reading or changing process memory, running commands as the PHP process user, or crashing the process.

A query builder component in a MongoDB integration library for a PHP web framework does not run the query-modification callbacks that an application registers with the framework before sending read, update, and delete operations to the database. As a result, a filter that an application relies on to limit which records a request may touch can be omitted silently. A user with basic application privileges may be able to read or change records that the application intended to keep out of reach.

A polymorphic relationship query helper in the MongoDB Eloquent integration for Laravel resolves a record's type identifier inconsistently between the code that stores a relationship link and the code that searches for one. An application that relies on a relationship-absence query to restrict which records a request may see or change can therefore have that restriction silently fail, allowing a user with basic application privileges to read and to modify or remove records the restriction was meant to cover.

A flaw was found in the file-gif-load plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted JIF image file, a 32-bit integer overflow occurs during the pixel buffer size calculation, while the zlib output limit is computed separately without wrapping. This leads to an undersized heap allocation, resulting in a heap-based buffer overflow when the compressed image data is decompressed. This issue can result in an application crash, leading to a denial of service, or potentially allow for arbitrary code execution.

A logic flaw in the query-building layer of the Mongoid object-document mapper causes a model-level default restriction that is meant to return no records to be silently discarded when it is combined into a query. A user with basic application privileges who sends an ordinary request may read, change, or remove records that the restriction was intended to withhold.

Improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions.



Because any user permitted to run the runbook selects which revision to run, this issue remains reachable in an affected Region until earlier revisions can no longer be run there. AWS is deprecating all revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) in every Region and partition beginning January 15, 2027; until deprecation, earlier revisions remain runnable, so upgrading alone is not sufficient.



To remediate this issue:



1. Run the latest revision of the runbook. The latest revision is the fixed revision in every Region where the runbook is available, and its revision number varies by Region. To find it, run aws ssm describe-document --name AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 --region <region> --query "Document.LatestVersion". Update any Automation executions, State Manager associations, AWS Config remediation configurations, or other automations pinned to an earlier revision to use the latest revision. 2. Until earlier revisions are removed in your Region, either keep untrusted users from running earlier revisions of the runbook, or keep a trusted Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in every Region. Earlier revisions inject only when they create this document, so while a trusted one exists, this path is closed in that Region. 3. Review your Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) in any Region where it was first created by an earlier revision of this runbook, not by you. To check, look for any run of this runbook that failed with "DOCUMENT CREATE OR UPDATE FAILED." An injected run always fails with this error. You can also compare the creation date of the document's first version with the start times of runs of this runbook in that Region. Check the document for settings you did not configure, especially shellProfile, Run As (runAsEnabled, runAsDefaultUser), maxSessionDuration, idleSessionTimeout, and the logging destination fields. The fixed runbook updates only the S3 bucket and prefix fields of an existing preferences document, so settings injected earlier remain until you remove them. If you find unexpected settings, restore your trusted preferences and review instances on which Session Manager sessions were started while those settings were active. The AWS Security Bulletin includes commands for this review.

paramz through 0.10.0 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted model files to paramz.load(), which calls pickle.load() without restrictions. Attackers can embed objects whose __reduce__ method returns callables like exec or os.system in shared paramz or GPy model files to run code with the victim's privileges.

Teracom TCW122B-CM firmware before 4.07 contains a predictable session cookie vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to hijack administrator sessions by guessing tick-counter-derived cookies. Attackers can predict or brute-force the 32-bit cookie from device uptime and login timing to control relays, settings, and administrator credentials.

Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::LoadMD5MeshFile() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via unvalidated weight ranges and bone indices. Attackers can supply a crafted .md5mesh file with out-of-range mBone values to increment heap words past the piCount allocation, causing memory corruption, out-of-bounds reads, or crashes.

ChargePoint Home Flex dwnldlogsm tar Command Injection Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the tar function. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied string before using it to execute a system call. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29057.

ChargePoint Home Flex uploadsm filetype Link Following Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the handling of the filetype parameter passed to the uploadsm endpoint. By creating a symbolic link, an attacker can abuse the service to write an arbitrary file. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29096.

ChargePoint Home Flex busybox Unnecessary Privileges Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of ChargePoint Home Flex EV chargers. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the busybox binary. The issue results from the setuid flag being set. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of root. Was ZDI-CAN-29090.

RustDesk Client for Windows reg_recovery Missing Authorization Local Privilege Escalation Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows local attackers to escalate privileges on affected installations of RustDesk Client for Windows. An attacker must first obtain the ability to execute low-privileged code on the target system in order to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the main IPC endpoint exposed by the RustDesk service. The issue results from the lack of authorization prior to allowing access to functionality. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to escalate privileges and execute arbitrary code in the context of SYSTEM. Was ZDI-CAN-34805.

To escape a bound parameter, or a name passed to a catalog function, psqlODBC has to know where each multibyte character of the client encoding ends. It treated a client encoding named by an alias the server accepts, such as WIN950, Windows950 or big-5 for BIG5, as single-byte, and it accepted too narrow a range of lead bytes for JOHAB, EUC_TW, EUC_CN and EUC_KR. A quote byte that the server reads as part of such a character was then not doubled, or a quote the server reads on its own was taken for part of a character, and the literal ended early.

An end user who controls one bound character parameter, or a name the application passes to a catalog function such as SQLTables(), can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. This requires a connection that is not in UTF-8: the ANSI driver, or the ANSI entry points, with one of these client encodings. For bound parameters the driver must also be substituting parameters itself, as it does with UseServerSidePrepare=0 or a cursor type other than forward-only.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC scans statement text itself to substitute parameters, translate ODBC escapes, join batched statements and rewrite queries for updatable cursors. Where it read the text differently from the server, text the driver took for data ran as SQL, or a positioned write went to another table:

- An escape string constant written e'…' in lower case was not recognised as one, and '…' after a keyword ending in E, as in LIKE'…', was taken for one.
- A } inside a quoted literal ended an ODBC {d …}, {t …}, {ts …} or {escape …} sequence.
- Dollar-quote tags containing _ were not recognised, and an identifier starting with _ followed by $, such as _$$, was taken for the start of a dollar quote, so a parameter marker inside a literal was substituted.
- A trailing -- comment in one statement of a batched parameter array swallowed the next statement.
- Comments, literals longer than 255 bytes and escape strings were misread when the driver located the FROM and WHERE clauses of a query for an updatable cursor, and the text copied into the cursor's own queries could include SQL from inside a literal.
- A table name containing $ was cut at the $, and a quoted table name starting with , or ; ended the table list, so positioned updates, inserts and deletes went to another table.
- An integer parameter with an embedded NUL byte cut the query short.
- /*/ was taken for a comment that opens and closes, while the server reads it as one that only opens.
- ConnSettings was split at every semicolon, including one inside a quoted literal, so an application that puts an end user's value into a SET command there ran the rest of the value as SQL at connect time.

An end user who controls text the application puts into a statement, or a parameter value, can run SQL with the rights of the application's database role. A database user who can create a table with a crafted name can redirect another user's positioned writes to a table of their choosing.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

psqlODBC parsed and built connection strings in ways that let a value end early:

- In a braced value, such as PWD={…}, a trailing byte 0x7d of a GBK, Big5 or SJIS character was taken for the closing brace.
- A braced value that ended right after an escaped }} was not reported as unterminated, and its contents were parsed as further keywords.
- SQLConnectW(), SQLDriverConnectW() and SQLBrowseConnectW() cut a connection string whose UTF-8 form is longer than 32767 bytes, which changes how the rest of it is parsed.
- On Windows with MSDTC, the password and user name were put into the XA open string without escaping, and the XA library copied each item of that string into a 64-byte stack buffer.
- Percent-encoding a long password wrote one byte past a 4096-byte stack buffer.

An end user who supplies a password, or another value the application puts into the connection string, can set other connection keywords, for example to connect the application to a server of their choosing. The MSDTC case can also overflow a stack buffer in the process that loads the XA library.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A SQL injection vulnerability exists in the Search Agents API of StellarOne due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input. An authenticated attacker with Viewer privileges can send crafted requests to manipulate backend SQL queries. This issue affects StellarOne: before 5.0.3232.

The Groundhogg plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery in versions up to, and including, 4.11 This is due to the Admin_Page::page() callback dispatching methods named directly by the $_REQUEST['action'] parameter via call_user_func([$this, $action]) without verifying a nonce: the only nonce check lives in process_action() (admin_init), which prefixes the action with 'process_' before dispatching, so an attacker who supplies action=process_delete causes process_action() to look up the nonexistent 'process_process_delete' method and bail without ever calling wp_verify_nonce(), while page() subsequently invokes the real process_delete() (and other process_* methods such as process_spam, process_status_change, process_edit) with no CSRF token of its own. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary contacts, change contact opt-in status (including marking contacts as spam, which also appends their IP to the site-wide disallowed_keys option), and perform other state-changing actions via a forged request granted they can trick a site administrator (or any user holding the relevant Groundhogg capability such as delete_contacts/edit_contacts) into performing an action such as clicking on a link.

The Secure MCP Server for Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Cursor and other AI Agents plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.8 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for attackers (with access to a valid MCP bearer token) to escalate privileges to the token owner's Administrator role — bypassing NHI ability allow-list and scope restrictions entirely — by submitting any valid MCP bearer token (including scope-restricted connection-test tokens) to arbitrary WordPress endpoints such as admin-ajax.php. This requires possession of a valid MCP bearer token, which is routinely issued to any administrator who connects an MCP client to the site. Successful exploitation causes the attacker's own account to receive the complete Administrator role.

Iceburg CRM through 5.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to modify any user record by supplying arbitrary record_id values to POST /data/save. Attackers can submit a save request for the ice_users module with the administrator's record_id to change their password or email and take over the account.

The App Builder – Create Native Android & iOS Apps On The Flight plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Authentication Bypass via Google ID Token Audience Validation Bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.7.1. This is due to the `LoginGoogle::login()` function failing to validate the `aud` (audience) claim of the supplied `idToken` against any OAuth client ID belonging to the WordPress site, failing to verify the `email_verified` claim, and resolving WordPress accounts solely by the email claim without binding to the Google `sub` (subject) identifier — while the `/app-builder/v1/login` REST endpoint is registered with a `permission_callback` that unconditionally returns `true`, leaving it fully reachable by unauthenticated requesters. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to authenticate as any existing WordPress user — including Administrators — whose email address is known, by supplying a Google-signed ID token obtained from an entirely unrelated OAuth client containing the target user's email claim, which causes the plugin to issue a signed App Builder JWT granting that user's full privileges. Exploitation requires the attacker to obtain a valid Google-signed ID token carrying the target user's email address, which can be achieved by operating a separate Google OAuth client and inducing the target user to authenticate through it.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a query injection vulnerability that allows low-privilege or anonymous users to inject AQL or SQL by supplying unescaped parameters to ArangoDB and Snowflake queries. Attackers can execute published queries with crafted parameter values to bypass filters, read entire datasources, and modify or delete all stored documents.

Budibase server from 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows view users and anonymous visitors to access entire base tables by passing a view id to the /api/:viewId/rows routes. Attackers can read, export, modify, and delete rows outside the view filter, including hidden columns, or read the full table unauthenticated through PUBLIC views.

Budibase before 4.0.0 contains a JSON injection vulnerability that allows attackers to inject JSON structure into S3 delete and Google Sheets row fields via unescaped template parameters. Attackers can submit crafted parameters to the queries endpoint to add extra Key entries, deleting chosen S3 objects or overriding Sheets row columns.

Coder before 2.29.27, 2.30.0 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 returns database connection errors containing a temporary AWS IAM database password in API key middleware responses. During database connection failures, unauthenticated attackers can send a well-formed but invalid API key to obtain the password and access the PostgreSQL database for 15 minutes.

ezdxf through 1.4.5 contains a code injection vulnerability in the dxf2code add-on that allows attackers to inject Python code via unescaped single quotes in DXF table entry names. Attackers can craft a DXF file whose layer, linetype, style, or appid names break out of quoted strings in generated scripts, executing code with the privileges of the user running them.

pyfda through 0.9.5 contains an insecure deserialization vulnerability in load_filter() that allows attackers to execute code by supplying crafted .npz or .pkl filter files.
