A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in the admin panel of PHPGurukul News Portal Project V4.1 allows remote attackers to hijack the authentication of administrators and perform unauthorized state-changing actions, such as adding, editing, or deleting posts and sub-admins, or changing passwords, via crafted HTTP requests. This occurs because the application fails to implement anti-CSRF tokens for admin actions and permits destructive operations via HTTP GET requests.

Netatalk is a Free and Open Source file server suite for Unix-like operating systems. From 3.1.0 until 4.5.0, sl_unpack_loop in etc/afpd/spotlight_marshalling.c uses an attacker-controlled Spotlight table-of-contents index during FPSpotlightRPC without checking it against the number of entries or the remaining dsi->commands buffer. An authenticated AFP client with access to a Spotlight-enabled volume can choose a large toc_index whose multiplication and addition produce an out-of-range address, causing an attacker-influenced heap read and reliably crashing the worker serving that session. The earlier CVE-2026-44066 remediation bounded recursion depth and toc_offset but did not bound toc_index. This issue is fixed in version 4.5.0.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.10, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.10.26 does not guard all execution paths of its database restore process against second-order SQL injection, allowing a Subscriber-level user who has stored crafted content in their own account to escalate to administrator when an administrator later restores a backup.
This is due to an incomplete fix of CVE-2026-108761 in 1.26.9: the fix guards only one of the restore routine's execution paths, and a second path remains exploitable.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not correctly handle comment-like content found in the middle of a long SQL statement when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber who have stored crafted content in their own profile to have SQL executed when an administrator later restores a backup, and so escalate their account to administrator.

This is a different code path from the backup restore issue fixed in 1.26.10, and it does not depend on the database server's maximum packet size.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not preserve long database values byte-for-byte when restoring a database backup, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant a serialized value that becomes a PHP Object Injection once an administrator backs up and restores the database.

No gadget chain is known in the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or WordPress core, so the demonstrated effect is instantiation of an attacker-chosen class in the attacker's own requests. Exploitation requires the planted data to line up exactly with how the backup is read back, which depends on details of the attacker's row and the database dump format.

The UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 do not keep a serialized value inert when their database search and replace reaches its recursion limit, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to plant data in their own user meta that is rewritten into a live PHP object when an administrator later runs a search and replace or a migration restore, and is then instantiated by WordPress on a later read.

This is distinct from CVE-2024-10957, whose fix restricted the unserialize call but left this path in place. No gadget chain is present in WordPress core or the UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 themselves; further impact depends on a suitable class from another installed UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 2.26.16.26, UpdraftPlus: WP Backup & Migration Plugin WordPress plugin before 1.26.16 or .

dsniff through 2.5a2 contains an integer underflow in decode_sniffer() in decode_sniffer.c that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write past the global obuf buffer. Attackers can send a UDP datagram to port 2001 on a monitored segment with a 4096-byte string, disabling base64_pton bounds checks to corrupt memory and crash dsniff.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in modplug_read_header() in libavformat/libmodplug.c that allocates the buffer using max_size instead of sz. When max_size is set to 0, attackers can supply crafted module files that avio_read() copies into a zero-sized buffer, causing memory corruption, crashes, or possible code execution.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ogg_buffer_data() in libavformat/oggenc.c because ogg_buffer_page() leaves a full page current after failed allocation. When page allocation fails, a memset with length (size_t)-1 or an overflowing memcpy writes past the segment table, causing heap memory corruption and crashes when writing Ogg output.

In Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK versions 2.0.0-milestone-10 to 2.0.0-milestone-16, the destination validation of the Operation Delegation feature, introduced to prevent server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-7412), can be bypassed through DNS rebinding.



Before dispatching a delegated Operation invocation, the server resolves the host of the `invocationDelegation` qualifier URI and rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast and cloud metadata addresses. The outbound HTTP client (Reactor Netty), however, performs its own, independent DNS lookup when opening the connection and does not use the validated addresses. An attacker who can create or update a Submodel Operation and controls the DNS records of the delegation host can answer the validation lookup with a public address and the connection lookup with an internal address. No authentication is required when the authorization feature is not enabled.



Invoking the Operation then causes the BaSyx server to send HTTP POST requests to destinations the protection is meant to block, such as services in internal IT/OT networks, loopback-only interfaces, or cloud metadata endpoints. The server can be used to pivot into network segments that are not directly reachable by the attacker.



Only deployments with the Operation Delegation feature enabled are affected. The feature is enabled by default.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Java Server SDK 2.0.0-milestone-17.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in the project REST API of Apache Texera (incubating).



The project API did not check that the caller owns, or has been granted access to, the project being accessed. Any authenticated user with an approved account (the REGULAR or ADMIN role; new accounts need administrator approval by default) could view, modify or delete other users' projects, change which workflows those projects contain, and see the e-mail addresses of a project's owner and collaborators. The project feature is hidden in the web UI by default, but the API was reachable regardless of that setting.



This issue affects Apache Texera: from 1.1.0-incubating before 1.3.0-incubating.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.3.0-incubating, which fixes the issue by removing the deprecated project feature and its data.



If you cannot upgrade immediately, configure the reverse proxy in front of Texera to reject every request whose path starts with /api/project, /api/public/project or /api/access/project, and every request whose path contains ';', which the Texera server ignores when routing. Respond with 403 or 404, not 401: from 1.2.0-incubating the web UI treats a 401 as an expired session, and the workflow pages request the project list when they load. Unless an administrator has enabled the project feature, this does not affect other functionality; those project-list requests are simply rejected. Make sure the Texera server is reachable only through that proxy.



Blocking and upgrading do not undo access obtained earlier. Before upgrading, review the project, project_user_access and workflow_of_project tables, which remain empty unless someone has used the feature, and remove rows you do not expect; the upgrade deletes these tables. Do not copy project grants into workflow_user_access without checking each one.

EpicStaff 1.2.0 before 1.3.1 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in DocumentViewSet download and copy endpoints that allows authenticated users to access other organizations' documents. Attackers holding Knowledge Sources permissions in one organization can enumerate sequential document IDs to download or copy foreign documents, or insert documents into another organization's collection.

PyTorch Foundation PyTorch PT2 File Parsing Exposed Dangerous Method Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected installations of PyTorch Foundation PyTorch. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of PT2 archive files. The issue results from an exposed dangerous function. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to execute code in the context of the current process. Was ZDI-CAN-32653.

VeraCrypt before 1.26.30 on Linux contains a command injection vulnerability in CoreUnix::CheckFilesystem that allows a local attacker with same-UID access and an active elevated CoreService session to execute arbitrary commands by injecting an unsanitized VirtualDevice value into a shell command string. Attackers can reopen the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> and supply a crafted VirtualDevice value such as /dev/null; <command> to achieve arbitrary command execution as root.

VeraCrypt through 1.26.31 on Linux contains an improper path restriction vulnerability in the elevated CoreService, which passes the path and owner UID from a SetFileOwnerRequest directly to chown() in CoreUnix::SetFileOwner without target validation on Linux. An attacker with an active elevated CoreService session and same-UID access who reopens the request pipe through /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> can take ownership of arbitrary system files such as /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow, achieving full root compromise.

pain001-mcp 0.0.72 before 0.0.80 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the commit_payment_batch MCP tool that allows attackers to write files outside any output directory via output_file_path. Attackers can stage a batch, reuse the self-issued confirmation_token, and supply absolute, dot-dot, or symlinked paths to create or overwrite server-writable files with generated XML.

Wails before 2.17.1 on Linux contains an origin validation error in the sendMessageToBackend WebKitGTK handler that allows child-frame scripts to invoke the privileged IPC channel. Attackers controlling content loaded in an iframe can post messages that pass the top-level URI origin check and call bound Go methods and Wails runtime operations.

Mastodon 4.7.4 and 4.8.0-alpha.3 before 5.0.0-beta.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in authenticate_with_sign_in_token that allows authenticated local users to rebind pending login attempts to other accounts. Attackers can submit sign_in_token_resend with a victim's user[email] parameter, then guess the unthrottled 6-character token to sign in as inactive accounts lacking two-factor authentication.

Ever Gauzy is an open source business management platform for ERP, CRM, HRM, ATS, and project management. Prior to 111.42.11, singleton-scoped ExportService stores the per-request identifiers this.idCsv and this.idZip as BehaviorSubjects and keeps derived directory names in instance fields, while singleton-scoped ImportService stores per-request paths in this._dirname and this._extractPath. Concurrent requests by different tenant administrators to /export, /export/template, /export/filter, or /import can interleave while asynchronous file operations are in progress, allowing one tenant's export archive to be delivered, overwritten, or deleted by another operation, or causing one tenant's import to read another tenant's uploaded CSV data and persist it under the wrong tenant. This issue is fixed in version 111.42.11.

OpenEXR is the reference implementation and specification for the EXR image format, widely used in the motion picture industry. From versions 3.4.0 through 3.4.18 and 3.5.0 through 3.5.2, decoding a crafted HT-compressed EXR chunk can cause ht_undo_impl() to write a 4-byte pixel value through a pointer that is not 4-byte aligned. This happens when the channels sum to a bytes-per-scanline stride that is not a multiple of four. This issue is fixed in versions 3.4.19 and 3.5.3.

EverOS before 1.8.0 contains a cross-origin local file disclosure vulnerability that allows malicious websites to read local files by abusing a wildcard CORS policy with credentials and unrestricted file:// ingestion. Attackers can host JavaScript that calls POST /api/v2/memory/add with file:// URIs, then read parsed contents via POST /api/v2/memory/search to exfiltrate SSH keys, credentials, and alter or delete memories.

Assimp before 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in MD5Importer::MakeDataUnique() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying unvalidated face indices. Attackers can craft an .md5mesh file with out-of-range face vertex indices or unfilled faces to set bits past the abHad allocation, read vertex data out of bounds, or crash the application.

metasfresh through 5.175 contains a SQL injection vulnerability in the stressTest_massCacheInvalidation handler of DebugRestController, which concatenates the caller-supplied tableName request parameter into SELECT statements without parameterization or validation and only checks that the caller is authenticated. Authenticated WebUI users with any role can send GET requests to /rest/api/debug/stressTest/massCacheInvalidation with SQL in the tableName parameter to run time-based and error-based blind queries against the PostgreSQL database, extracting sensitive ERP data such as user credentials and financial records while also degrading availability through sleep payloads.

A flaw was found in ironic-image. The scripts responsible for constructing kernel parameters for CoreOS root file system (rootfs) and Ignition configuration URLs use a hardcoded `http://` scheme. This bypasses the intended Transport Layer Security (TLS) protection, even when TLS is enabled for the iPXE boot chain. An attacker on the local network segment can exploit this vulnerability by performing Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) spoofing to serve a malicious rootfs or intercept sensitive data, including SSH keys and secrets, from the Ignition configuration. This leads to a compromise of data integrity and confidentiality during the node provisioning process.

To build positioned updates and to describe columns, psqlODBC matches the names in a statement against the catalog. Where it matched differently from the server, it used another table or column:

- Table and schema names were compared case-insensitively in its column-information cache, so users could be taken for another user's "Users", and the driver then evaluated that table's column default to answer @@IDENTITY.
- In FROM ONLY t, ONLY was taken for the table name.
- Column names were compared case-insensitively, so with Parse=1 the type of another column could decide the size of the application's buffer, which a fetch then overflowed.
- In a database whose encoding is single-byte, such as LATIN1 or SQL_ASCII, the server folds the accented letters of an unquoted name by its own locale, while the driver folded only A-Z, so ÉTAT could be taken for another user's "État" instead of état.
- On systems other than Windows, in a Turkish or Azeri locale, an unquoted I was not folded to i, and keywords and ODBC function names did not match.
- Without a schema name, SQLSpecialColumns() could report the key columns of another user's same-named temporary table, and SQLPrimaryKeys() could take another user's index named <table>_pkey for the primary key of a table without one.
- After search_path changed other than through a plain SET statement, positioned writes went to the same-named table in the previously current schema.
- SQLBulkOperations() trusted the ctid stored inside a variable-length bookmark handed back by the application, and ignored the WHERE clause that restricted the cursor, so a forged bookmark read, updated or deleted any row of the cursor's table.

A database user who can create a table in a schema on another user's search_path can redirect that user's positioned updates, inserts and deletes to a table of their choosing, where they run with the victim's rights, or run an expression of their choosing under the victim's role.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

ICU4C through 79.1 contains a use-after-free and double free vulnerability in the x11-compound-text converter because cloning shares the extraInfo block without a safeClone handler. A flaw was found in tuned. This vulnerability allows local privilege escalation because the spindown-disk profile script does not properly validate filesystem mount sources before executing remount operations with root privileges. A local user capable of creating user-space filesystems can craft a malicious mount entry to execute arbitrary commands as root.

A flaw was found in JBoss Enterprise Application Platform. The `processInvocation` function within the `org.jboss.as.ejb3.security.AuthorizationInterceptor` component incorrectly authorizes all requests when no roles are defined for an Enterprise Java Beans (EJB) method invocation. This allows attackers to bypass intended access restrictions for EJB methods, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive functionalities.

In Airflow versions prior to 1.10.13, when creating a user using airflow CLI, the password gets logged in plain text in the Log table in Airflow Metadatase. Same happened when creating a Connection with a password field.

Improper Access Control on Configurations Endpoint for the Stable API of Apache Airflow allows users with Viewer or User role to get Airflow Configurations including sensitive information even when `[webserver] expose_config` is set to `False` in `airflow.cfg`. This allowed a privilege escalation attack. This issue affects Apache Airflow 2.0.0.

In Apache Airflow prior to 2.2.0. This CVE applies to a specific case where a User who has "can_create" permissions on DAG Runs can create Dag Runs for dags that they don't have "edit" permissions for.

A race condition vulnerability was found in the vmwgfx driver in the Linux kernel. The flaw exists within the handling of GEM objects. The issue results from improper locking when performing operations on an object. This flaw allows a local privileged user to disclose information in the context of the kernel.

A double-free vulnerability was found in handling vmw_buffer_object objects in the vmwgfx driver in the Linux kernel. This issue occurs due to the lack of validating the existence of an object prior to performing further free operations on the object, which may allow a local privileged user to escalate privileges and execute code in the context of the kernel.

A flaw was found in libvirt. The virStoragePoolObjListSearch function does not return a locked pool as expected, resulting in a race condition and denial of service when attempting to lock the same object from another thread. This issue could allow clients connecting to the read-only socket to crash the libvirt daemon.

A sensitive information exposure vulnerability was found in foreman. Contents of tomcat's server.xml file, which contain passwords to candlepin's keystore and truststore, were found to be world readable.

LibTIFF is vulnerable to an integer overflow. This flaw allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly execute an arbitrary code via a crafted tiff image, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

A vulnerability was found in libtiff due to multiple potential integer overflows in raw2tiff.c. This flaw allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service or possibly execute an arbitrary code via a crafted tiff image, which triggers a heap-based buffer overflow.

A flaw was found in the IPv4 Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) classifier in the Linux kernel. The xprt pointer may go beyond the linear part of the skb, leading to an out-of-bounds read in the `rsvp_classify` function. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system and cause a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel. The xt_u32 module did not validate the fields in the xt_u32 structure. This flaw allows a local privileged attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds read by setting the size fields with a value beyond the array boundaries, leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Samba. It is susceptible to a vulnerability where multiple incompatible RPC listeners can be initiated, causing disruptions in the AD DC service. When Samba's RPC server experiences a high load or unresponsiveness, servers intended for non-AD DC purposes (for example, NT4-emulation "classic DCs") can erroneously start and compete for the same unix domain sockets. This issue leads to partial query responses from the AD DC, causing issues such as "The procedure number is out of range" when using tools like Active Directory Users. This flaw allows an attacker to disrupt AD DC services.

A vulnerability was discovered in Samba, where the flaw allows SMB clients to truncate files, even with read-only permissions when the Samba VFS module "acl_xattr" is configured with "acl_xattr:ignore system acls = yes". The SMB protocol allows opening files when the client requests read-only access but then implicitly truncates the opened file to 0 bytes if the client specifies a separate OVERWRITE create disposition request. The issue arises in configurations that bypass kernel file system permissions checks, relying solely on Samba's permissions.

A vulnerability was found in Samba's "rpcecho" development server, a non-Windows RPC server used to test Samba's DCE/RPC stack elements. This vulnerability stems from an RPC function that can be blocked indefinitely. The issue arises because the "rpcecho" service operates with only one worker in the main RPC task, allowing calls to the "rpcecho" server to be blocked for a specified time, causing service disruptions. This disruption is triggered by a "sleep()" call in the "dcesrv_echo_TestSleep()" function under specific conditions. Authenticated users or attackers can exploit this vulnerability to make calls to the "rpcecho" server, requesting it to block for a specified duration, effectively disrupting most services and leading to a complete denial of service on the AD DC. The DoS affects all other services as "rpcecho" runs in the main RPC task.

A flaw was found in wildfly-core. A management user could use the resolve-expression in the HAL Interface to read possible sensitive information from the Wildfly system. This issue could allow a malicious user to access the system and obtain possible sensitive information from the system.

A flaw was found in CRI-O that involves an experimental annotation leading to a container being unconfined. This may allow a pod to specify and get any amount of memory/cpu, circumventing the kubernetes scheduler and potentially resulting in a denial of service in the node.

A null pointer dereference flaw was found in the hugetlbfs_fill_super function in the Linux kernel hugetlbfs (HugeTLB pages) functionality. This issue may allow a local user to crash the system or potentially escalate their privileges on the system.

A Marvin vulnerability side-channel leakage was found in the RSA decryption operation in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a network attacker to decrypt ciphertexts or forge signatures, limiting the services that use that private key.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver and causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver, causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's NVMe driver. This issue may allow an unauthenticated malicious actor to send a set of crafted TCP packages when using NVMe over TCP, leading the NVMe driver to a NULL pointer dereference in the NVMe driver, causing kernel panic and a denial of service.

A vulnerability in the Eclipse Vert.x toolkit results in a memory leak due to using Netty FastThreadLocal data structures. Specifically, when the Vert.x HTTP client establishes connections to different hosts, triggering the memory leak. The leak can be accelerated with intimate runtime knowledge, allowing an attacker to exploit this vulnerability. For instance, a server accepting arbitrary internet addresses could serve as an attack vector by connecting to these addresses, thereby accelerating the memory leak.
A vulnerability was found in jberet-core logging. An exception in 'dbProperties' might display user credentials such as the username and password for the database-connection.

A vulnerability was found in GNU Nano that allows a possible privilege escalation through an insecure temporary file. If Nano is killed while editing, a file it saves to an emergency file with the permissions of the running user provides a window of opportunity for attackers to escalate privileges through a malicious symlink.
A flaw was found in OpenJPEG. A resource exhaustion can occur in the opj_t1_decode_cblks function in tcd.c through a crafted image file, causing a denial of service.

A vulnerability was found in Keycloak. This flaw allows attackers to bypass brute force protection by exploiting the timing of login attempts. By initiating multiple login requests simultaneously, attackers can exceed the configured limits for failed attempts before the system locks them out. This timing loophole enables attackers to make more guesses at passwords than intended, potentially compromising account security on affected systems.

A vulnerability was found in Podman, Buildah, and CRI-O. A symlink traversal vulnerability in the containers/storage library can cause Podman, Buildah, and CRI-O to hang and result in a denial of service via OOM kill when running a malicious image using an automatically assigned user namespace (`--userns=auto` in Podman and Buildah). The containers/storage library will read /etc/passwd inside the container, but does not properly validate if that file is a symlink, which can be used to cause the library to read an arbitrary file on the host.

A flaw was found in the HAL Console in the Wildfly component, which does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output used as a web page that is served to other users. The attacker must be authenticated as a user that belongs to management groups “SuperUser”, “Admin”, or “Maintainer”.

A vulnerability was found in CRI-O. A path traversal issue in the log management functions (UnMountPodLogs and LinkContainerLogs) may allow an attacker with permissions to create and delete Pods to unmount arbitrary host paths, leading to node-level denial of service by unmounting critical system directories.

A vulnerability has been identified in the libarchive library. This flaw can lead to a heap buffer over-read due to the size of a filter block potentially exceeding the Lempel-Ziv-Storer-Schieber (LZSS) window. This means the library may attempt to read beyond the allocated memory buffer, which can result in unpredictable program behavior, crashes (denial of service), or the disclosure of sensitive information from adjacent memory regions.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Shinetheme Traveler traveler allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Traveler: from n/a through 3.2.6.

A flaw was found in the Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Event-Driven Ansible (EDA) Event Stream API. This vulnerability allows exposure of sensitive client credentials and internal infrastructure headers via the test_headers field when an event stream is in test mode. The possible outcome includes leakage of internal infrastructure details, accidental disclosure of user or system credentials, privilege escalation if high-value tokens are exposed, and persistent sensitive data exposure to all users with read access on the event stream.

A flaw was found in the Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Event-Driven Ansible (EDA) Event Streams. This vulnerability allows an authenticated user to gain access to sensitive internal infrastructure headers (such as X-Trusted-Proxy and X-Envoy-*) and event stream URLs via crafted requests and job templates. By exfiltrating these headers, an attacker could spoof trusted requests, escalate privileges, or perform malicious event injection.

A flaw was found in the Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform Gateway route creation component. This vulnerability allows credential theft via the creation of misleading routes using a double-slash (//) prefix in the gateway_path. A malicious or socially engineered administrator can configure a honey-pot route to intercept and exfiltrate user credentials, potentially maintaining persistent access or creating a backdoor even after their permissions are revoked.

A flaw was found in libsoup. An integer underflow vulnerability occurs when processing content with a zero-length resource, leading to a buffer overread. This can allow an attacker to potentially access sensitive information or cause an application level denial of service.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An administrator with `manage-clients` permission can exploit a misconfiguration where this permission is equivalent to `manage-permissions`. This allows the administrator to escalate privileges and gain control over roles, users, or other administrative functions within the realm. This privilege escalation can occur when admin permissions are enabled at the realm level.

A flaw was found in virtio-win. The `RhelDoUnMap()` function does not properly validate the number of descriptors provided by a user during an unmap request. A local user could exploit this input validation vulnerability by supplying an excessive number of descriptors, leading to a buffer overrun. This can cause a system crash, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A flaw was found in virtio-win, specifically within the VirtIO Block (BLK) device. When the device undergoes a reset, it fails to properly manage memory, resulting in a use-after-free vulnerability. This issue could allow a local attacker to corrupt system memory, potentially leading to system instability or unexpected behavior.

A flaw was found in FFmpeg. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a specially crafted MPEG-PS/VOB media file containing a malicious DVD subtitle stream. This vulnerability is caused by a signed integer overflow in the DVD subtitle parser's fragment reassembly bounds checks, leading to a heap out-of-bounds write. Successful exploitation can result in a denial of service (DoS) due to an application crash, and potentially lead to arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated client could exploit an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability in the Authorization Services Protection API endpoint. By knowing or obtaining a resource's unique identifier (UUID) belonging to another Resource Server within the same realm, the client could bypass authorization checks. This allows the client to perform unauthorized GET, PUT, and DELETE operations on resources, leading to information disclosure and potential unauthorized modification or deletion of data.

A flaw was found in Samba’s vfs_worm module. The module is intended to provide write-once, read-many (WORM) protections by preventing modification of files after a configurable grace period. Due to insufficient validation during rename operations, an authenticated user with write access to a share could overwrite a protected file by renaming a newly created file over the existing WORM-protected file.
Leftover debug modules contain fixed credentials for internal AWS Cognito test sandboxes, risking asset exploitation.
Weak validation logic within device dissociation API routines allows a remote entity to forcefully unbind unrelated user endpoints, causing severe denial of service.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in FFmpeg's RASC video decoder. The decode_move() function initializes a read pointer into a decompressed buffer, but a subsequent reallocation of that same buffer during move-table processing leaves the pointer dangling. An attacker could exploit this by providing a specially crafted AVI file containing a malicious RASC video stream. When a user opens or plays the file, the decoder reads from freed heap memory, which could lead to a denial of service (crash).

A flaw was found in the libblkid library of util-linux. During nested partition probing, the BSD, Minix, Solaris x86, and UnixWare partition probers cache a raw pointer to a parent partition entry in a dynamically allocated array. When subsequent partition additions cause the array to be reallocated, this pointer becomes stale, leading to a heap use-after-free read. An attacker who can present a crafted block device image (for example, via USB insertion or a loop-mounted disk image) can trigger this flaw without user interaction, as libblkid is invoked automatically by udev/udisks as root on block-device hot-plug events. This could lead to limited information disclosure or denial of service.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. A highly privileged user with `manage-clients` permission can exploit this vulnerability by injecting a hardcoded role mapper into any client. This action allows the user to bypass existing scope restrictions and inject the `realm-admin` role into generated tokens, resulting in privilege escalation and full administrative access to the realm.

A flaw was found in Foreman. This broken access control vulnerability allows an authenticated user with host-edit permissions to retarget an existing lookup value override to a different host. This is achieved by modifying the match field through nested host attributes, effectively bypassing authorisation checks. The consequence is the potential for unauthorised modification of managed host configurations across different organisational and location boundaries.

A flaw was found in foreman. Authenticated users with 'view_keypairs' permission can bypass taxonomy scoping, allowing them to download private SSH (Secure Shell) keys from other organizations by directly querying key pair IDs. This vulnerability leads to cross-tenant data exposure in multi-tenant deployments, potentially compromising sensitive information.

A flaw was found in Jastow. Jastow is vulnerable to Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack. If using a set of combined configuration to allow unescaped characters in URL with embedded Undertow and Jastow, a server might be vulnerable to improper input handling.

A flaw was found in openshift/oauth-proxy. On paths configured to bypass authentication (skip-auth-regex), the proxy forwards client-supplied identity headers (X-Forwarded-User, X-Forwarded-Email, X-Forwarded-Access-Token) to the upstream application without stripping them. An unauthenticated attacker can inject forged identity headers on whitelisted paths.

A flaw was found in JSS (Java Security Services). The JSSTrustManager class does not verify NSS trust flags when validating CA certificates, allowing certificates present in the NSS database without TRUSTED_CA flags to be accepted as trust anchors for TLS connections. In non-default configurations where certificate revocation checking is disabled, this could allow a man-in-the-middle attacker to forge certificates accepted by PKI client connections.

A flaw was found in file-roller. When opening or extracting a malicious 7z or RAR archive containing a file entry with an excessively long path, file-roller's progress-line parsing copies the path into a fixed-size stack buffer using an unbounded string copy. This can trigger a stack buffer overflow and cause file-roller to terminate, resulting in a denial of service. To exploit this flaw, a victim must open or extract the crafted archive using file-roller.

A flaw was found in 389-ds-base. A remote, authenticated attacker could exploit a vulnerability in the Simple Authentication and Security Layer (SASL) UNBIND process. By sending a specially crafted request, the attacker can cause a connection to stall, leading to resource exhaustion and a Denial of Service (DoS) for the server.

A flaw was found in Foreman. The template revision endpoint does not enforce object-level authorization when retrieving an audited template revision. An authenticated, low privileged user with a template-related permission, such as view_ptables, can obtain historical template contents belonging to another organization or location by supplying the corresponding audit ID. This can result in unauthorized disclosure of historical template contents, which may contain sensitive configuration information, credentials, or other secrets. The REST API revision endpoints correctly restrict this lookup.

The MongoDB Go Driver's client-level bulk write operation may accept a caller-supplied database name containing a reserved separator character without escaping it before the name is used to build the target namespace for the operation. An application that passes untrusted input as a database name could therefore have the write directed at a database and collection other than the ones it intended. Only the Client.BulkWrite API is affected.

A flaw was found in Netty. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending a specially crafted HTTP request that includes control characters within the chunk-size line. This bypasses the intended strict validation, allowing the attacker to inject arbitrary HTTP requests. This vulnerability can lead to HTTP request smuggling, potentially resulting in information disclosure or other unauthorized actions.

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/1.1 decoder. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass `Transfer-Encoding` header validation by splitting the `Transfer-Encoding` field across multiple headers, with the last field containing a non-final transfer coding like `gzip` or `deflate`. This bypass can lead to HTTP request smuggling, enabling attackers to bypass security controls, desynchronize request processing, or cause requests to be processed in an unintended context.

A flaw was found in pppd. A remote attacker could exploit a buffer overflow vulnerability in the PEAP response handling. By sending a specially crafted PEAP Request packet, an attacker could cause the pppd process to corrupt global static data, leading to incorrect behavior or a system crash.

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/2 stack. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to inject prohibited characters, such as NUL, Line Feed, and Carriage Return, into HTTP/2 header field values due to insufficient validation. When these values cross an HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 translation boundary, they can be exploited for request smuggling, header injection, or response splitting. This could lead to unauthorized access, data manipulation, or other security bypasses.

A flaw was found in Netty's HTTP/1 decoder. Incomplete validation of malformed Transfer-Encoding headers allows a remote attacker to perform HTTP request smuggling. By sending specially crafted HTTP requests, an attacker can inject arbitrary HTTP requests, potentially bypassing security controls or accessing unauthorized resources.

A flaw was found in Netty's `netty-codec-http` component. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted HTTP/1.1 chunk-size token that includes post-digit whitespace. This incorrect parsing of the chunk size can lead to HTTP request smuggling. This allows an attacker to bypass security controls or access unauthorized resources in proxy/backend deployments.

If a malicious SDK container declares an extension point with a crafted `directory` path, and a developer runs `flatpak build-init --writable-sdk --sdk-extension` with that SDK, attacker-chosen files could be written outside the working directory, since the target path is resolved via a function that allows `..` traversal.

A malicious OCI registry can hardlink arbitrary host files into the extraction directory when a user installs or updates a Flatpak application from an OCI remote, allowing disclosure of arbitrary host file contents. For system-wide installs running as root, this includes sensitive files such as /etc/shadow.

A flaw was found in rubygem-hammer_cli. A command injection vulnerability exists in Hammer CLI and the Railties (Ruby on Rails) component distributed with Satellite due to the insecure interpolation of the $EDITOR environment variable into the Ruby system() method. By passing a single interpolated string to system(), the application invokes a system shell (/bin/sh) that interprets shell metacharacters (e.g., ;, |, &).

A flaw has been found in **permission filters** in the **foreman** package. The API loads a filter by its identifier and does not apply the search limit on the caller's permission. A low-privileged network attacker or user must already be allowed to delete filters for one role only. They can delete filters that belong to other unlocked roles. Those other roles then lose the access the deleted filters had granted.
Out-of-bounds read in Microsoft Bluetooth Driver allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.

A flaw was found in Nautilus. When a removable drive or disk image is unmounted or ejected, Nautilus prompts the user to empty the trash without verifying whether the trash directory paths are symbolic links. An attacker can exploit this flaw by tricking a user into mounting a crafted storage volume and confirming the prompt to empty the trash, leading to the arbitrary deletion of files accessible to that user.

A flaw was found in the GStreamer ASF demuxer in gst-plugins-ugly. When parsing a Simple Index object, an attacker-controlled entry count is used to size a heap allocation without being limited to the payload available in the object. Processing a crafted ASF, WMV, or WMA file can cause a very large memory allocation request and lead to denial of service if the allocation fails or the process is memory-constrained.

The system certificate authority (CA) store in Red Hat products, distributed via ca-certificates RPM packages, included multiple root CA certificates of authorities, which signed intermediate CA certificates with weak private keys issued by the eMudhra certificate authority. A man-in-the-middle attacker could use this flaw to issue certificates for arbitrary host names signed by the weak intermediate CA certificates, which would be considered trusted by a TLS/SSL client using system CA store and cause such clients to connect to malicious sites.

Due to inability to only distrust specific intermediate certificates in all clients using the system CA store, root CA certificates of authorities that signed weak intermediate CA certificates are being removed.

A flaw was found in the platform-mbean component of JBoss EAP, which provides management access to JVM-level metrics and configurations. The issue occurs because the handler for the read-resource operation on the runtime management resource fails to perform required Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) checks. This allows an authenticated user with low-privileged access, such as the Monitor role, to view sensitive system properties and JVM configuration details that should be restricted.

A flaw was found in ansible-core's ansible.builtin.git module. The module
invokes git (ls-remote, clone, fetch) with the repository URL as a positional
argument and without a "--" separator, so a repository URL that begins with a
dash is interpreted by git as a command-line option. A caller that passes an
attacker-controlled repository URL to the module can trigger argument
injection (for example --upload-pack/--exec), resulting in arbitrary command
execution on the host running the module.

This issue was addressed by removing the vulnerable code. This issue is fixed in HomeView Software Version 27.2, iOS 26.7.3 and iPadOS 26.7.3, iOS 27.2.1 and iPadOS 27.2.1, macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.3, macOS Tahoe 26.7.3, visionOS 27.2.1, watchOS 27.2.1. A user added to an iMessage group may be able to access messages sent before they joined.
Untrusted pointer dereference in Windows Security Account Manager allows an authorized attacker to deny service over a network.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Kernel allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.
Use after free in Windows Print Spooler Components allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.
Use after free in Windows Kernel allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.
Untrusted pointer dereference in Windows Storage allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.
Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Kernel allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges with a physical attack.
Improper certificate validation in Windows Hyper-V allows an authorized attacker to bypass a security feature locally.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated general administrators to inject arbitrary SQL by setting the personsSort session value, which is concatenated unsanitized into ORDER BY clauses in MdlUser.php and MdlSpace.php. Attackers can submit an error-based extractvalue payload through personsSort to leak database information, such as the MariaDB version, via the user and space listing pages.
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS in the GitHub App repository selector was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS in the Commit Status Publisher settings was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS on the thread dump page was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored and reflected XSS in Space project connection dialogs was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS in the JaCoCo coverage settings was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 a DOM-based XSS in the plugin installation dialog was possible
In JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.2.1, 2026.1.5 stored XSS in the Create Project dialog was possible

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.7, POST /api/auth/2fa/verify-temp in api/server/routes/auth.js calls verify2FAWithTempToken and accepts repeated TOTP or backup-code guesses without a dedicated attempt limiter. An attacker must first possess valid primary credentials and a valid five-minute temp token, but can then make repeated second-factor attempts and obtain a full session if a valid code is guessed. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.7.

LibreChat is an enhanced ChatGPT clone that supports multiple AI providers. Prior to 0.8.6, POST /api/messages/:conversationId authorizes req.params.conversationId in api/server/middleware/validateMessageReq.js but persists attacker-controlled req.body.conversationId through api/server/routes/messages.js. An authenticated attacker can use an owned conversation in the URL while naming a victim conversation in the body, causing an attacker-controlled message to be stored in the victim conversation. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.6.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not escape the error message returned when a remote feed cannot be retrieved before outputting it, which could allow users with the contributor role and above to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks against administrators by pointing the feed at a server they control.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust CPU by supplying unbounded business-day operands in datemath filters. Attackers can send task or time-tracking filters like due_date > now+999999999999b, triggering a per-day loop in go-datemath that pins CPU cores and exhausts the server.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated CalDAV users to exhaust server CPU by uploading VTODO properties with many parameters. Attackers can PUT an iCalendar body with thousands of parameters on one line to any valid project ID, triggering superlinear parsing before permission checks.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. Attackers can submit a query summing or multiplying large decimal literals or aggregate stored decimals with GROUP ALL, causing a rust_decimal panic that terminates the entire server process.

SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check_update_permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.

actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.

Frappe ERPNext 7.0.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in endpoints that build part of a query from caller-supplied sort parameters without validation. Authenticated low-privilege users can send crafted requests whose sort parameter holds SQL that the database executes as part of the query, extracting sensitive information.

Hysteria 1.0.0 before 2.9.2 contains a denial of service vulnerability in FragUDPMessage where UDP fragmentation fails to handle headers larger than the maximum datagram payload size. Authenticated clients can advertise a small max_datagram_frame_size and trigger a UDP response, causing a slice bounds panic that crashes the server.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the XMT scene loader that allows attackers to access freed heap memory by supplying a crafted XMT file. When xmt_parse_element() replaces an SFNode field child, the freed node stays cached in parser->peeked_nodes and a later DEF lookup passes it to gf_node_get_name(), crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() in src/scene_manager/loader_xmt.c that writes to freed heap memory when replacing single-node field commands. Attackers can persuade users to process a crafted XMT file where a Conditional node owning the command is unregistered, corrupting heap memory and crashing MP4Box.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in the BT/XMT context loader that frees an interaction-type decoder-specific descriptor even when UIConfig re-encoding fails. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene with a BIFSConfig descriptor, causing gf_odf_delete_descriptor() to reuse and free it again, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability because xmt_find_node() in loader_xmt.c resolves DEF names without verifying the node belongs to the current scene graph. Attackers can craft an XMT scene reusing a PROTO node across graphs, causing gf_node_unregister() to read freed memory during teardown, crashing MP4Box and corrupting heap memory.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in xmt_node_end() that leaves freed child node MFURL fields in the OD link list. Attackers can supply a crafted XMT file with an extra top-level SceneReplace node, causing xmt_resolve_od_links() to read freed memory, crashing MP4Box and corrupting the heap.

In HandleRxPacket of logical_link.cc, there is a possible resource exhaustion due to a missing limit on packets buffered for channels that are never opened. This could lead to remote (proximal/adjacent) denial of service with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

Missing authorization in the Elastic AI Assistant for Security in Kibana can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global Security AI Assistant conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in build_frame_code() in libavformat/nutenc.c that allows attackers to corrupt the header_len[] array by supplying inputs with many audio streams. Attackers can remux a crafted input with many audio streams to NUT, causing out-of-bounds reads past static header tables and crashing the application.

SolarWinds Serv-U was found to be affected by a 
vulnerability allowing an attacker to repeatedly attempt 
authentication due to insufficient protection against 
password brute-force attacks.

Spug before 4.1.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrator users to read per-host SSH private keys through the GET /api/host/ endpoint. Users granted a host can read the cleartext pkey field returned by Host.to_view and log in directly over SSH, bypassing Spug's permissions and audit trail even after revocation.

GPAC through 26.07.0 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in SDP_ParseAttribute that allows attackers to cause unbounded memory growth via a NUL byte in an a=fmtp line. Attackers can supply a crafted .sdp file or malicious RTSP DESCRIBE response to hang gf_sdp_info_parse and exhaust memory, causing denial of service.

BusyBox ftpd Directory Traversal Arbitrary File Read and Write Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create or delete arbitrary files or disclose sensitive information on affected installations of BusyBox. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the ftpd service, which listens on TCP port 21 by default. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of a user-supplied path prior to using it in file operations. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create or delete files or disclose information in the context of the service account. Was ZDI-CAN-27555.

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/Search/SearchHighlighter.php. This issue affects MediaWiki: from 1.43.0 before 1.43.12, from 1.45.0 before 1.45.7, from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation MediaWiki. This vulnerability is associated with program files includes/Media/PNGMetadataExtractor.php. This issue affects MediaWiki: from 1.43.0 before 1.43.12, from 1.45.0 before 1.45.7, from 1.46.0 before 1.46.3, 1.47.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.3.4 before 0.11.0, LLM and other dynamically priced blocks run without charge when a priced input is left at its schema default. An account with a credit balance of zero can make unlimited language-model, code-generation, and image-generation calls at the operator's expense while the platform records the usage at zero cost. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.10.0, the format Jinja filter in TextFormatter accepts an unbounded width. An authenticated user who can author or run a workflow, or supply its input, can trigger a single synchronous multi-gigabyte allocation that exhausts the executor worker's memory and degrades or denies execution for other users. There is no confidentiality or integrity impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.10.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From 0.4.2 before 0.11.0, the E2B code-execution blocks ExecuteCodeBlock, InstantiateCodeSandboxBlock, and ClaudeCodeBlock can leave sandboxes running on the operator's shared E2B credential for up to the sandbox's full timeout, while users are billed only for the block's run time. Any user with a positive credit balance can keep sandboxes running for up to 24 hours on a Pro plan for a flat 1 credit, and each run adds another sandbox. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.11.0, template rendering is not bounded in size or time. Any signed-up user who can reach a block that takes a format string, such as Fill Text Template or Agent Output, through POST /api/blocks/{id}/execute or the external API's block-execute route, can make the REST API process allocate without bound with one request of a few dozen bytes. This can stop the process from answering any request, including its health check. There is no data read or change impact. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.0.

A flaw was found in the keycloak-services component of Keycloak, which is used for managing authentication and authorization flows. The issue occurs when a client policy is configured to enforce a high-assurance authentication flow requiring OTP. Due to improper validation of existing sessions, a lower-assurance password-only SSO session can be incorrectly accepted if the request does not explicitly demand a specific assurance level. This allows an attacker with access to a user's password or session to bypass the second factor and obtain tokens claiming a higher level of security.

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-bad mxfdemux handling of MXF Index Table Segment data. Crafted index metadata can lead to an out-of-range lookup during a seek and terminate the media process. A Fedora 43 test reproduced an assertion-triggered abort. The upstream advisory also notes possible information disclosure, but an attacker-visible leak has not been demonstrated.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak Operator. Deterministic hashes derived from Kubernetes Secrets are published in generated StatefulSet metadata and in KeycloakOIDCClient status. A user with read access to those resources may be able to recover a low-entropy credential referenced by a Secret, even when Kubernetes RBAC denies the user access to the Secret itself.

lightNVR before 0.44.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in go2rtc_proxy_authorize_request() that allows authenticated users to access restricted cameras by exploiting inconsistent src parameter parsing. Attackers can percent-encode a second src parameter name or exceed the 255-byte truncation so go2rtc resolves a different camera, obtaining unauthorized snapshots and HLS live streams.

ai-memory 2.6.0 before 3.3.2 contains a symlink following vulnerability in the ai-memory-wikisync companion that allows local attackers to overwrite arbitrary files by planting symlinks at predictable temporary names. Attackers can place a .wikisync-tmp-<page>.md symlink in a shared destination so atomic_write() truncates and overwrites its target with the victim's privileges.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in generic_ldap_connect in ldap-client-lib.pl that accepts any LDAPS or StartTLS server certificate. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the LDAP server to capture the bind DN password, often the root DN, and return forged directory data.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in connect_ldap_db in ldap-server/ldap-server-lib.pl that sends the LDAP root DN password unencrypted when encryption is set to Detect automatically. Passive network attackers observing traffic between Webmin and a remote LDAP server can capture directory root credentials because the connection loop always reaches a plaintext bind attempt.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in switch_smtp_to_ssl in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl and status/smtp-monitor.pl, which calls Net::SSLeay::connect without certificate verification or a hostname check. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate when SMTP with SSL or STARTTLS is configured to capture SMTP AUTH credentials and message content.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in ldap-client/check.cgi that allows LDAP directory writers to execute commands via unquoted uid values. Attackers can create a posixAccount entry with shell metacharacters in its uid, executing commands as root when an administrator runs Check Configuration.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a STARTTLS downgrade vulnerability in send_mail in mailboxes/boxes-lib.pl that continues over plaintext when STARTTLS is rejected. Man-in-the-middle attackers can strip or reject STARTTLS to capture configured SMTP AUTH credentials, crackable CRAM-MD5 exchanges, and the content of sent mail.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in imap_login in mailboxes/folders-lib.pl that skips certificate verification and hostname checks for IMAP SSL connections. Man-in-the-middle attackers can present any certificate to capture IMAP credentials sent by the System and Server Status IMAP monitor and spoof monitor results.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in password_change.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to change passwords for accounts with empty stored hashes. When passwd_mode is 2, attackers can POST user, old, new1 and new2 with any old value to set a known password and gain access.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a cleartext transmission vulnerability in the SMTP service monitor that never issues STARTTLS because get_smtp_status tests an undefined $ssl variable. Passive network attackers can capture AUTH PLAIN credentials sent in plaintext each time a STARTTLS-configured monitor runs, without needing a Webmin login.

A **NULL pointer dereference** flaw has been found in the acl_check_dns_host_name() and acl_validate_spn_value() functions in source4/dsdb/samdb/ldb_modules/acl.c of the Active Directory domain controller ACL module in the **Samba** package. The checks read the account name after a request that removes it, and they do not test that the value is present. A low-privileged network attacker or user who can update the DNS host name or service principal name of their own computer account can include a removal of sAMAccountName in that same LDAP modify. The directory process crashes. Repeating the modify keeps the directory service unavailable.

A security flaw has been discovered in NASA Core Flight System Limit Checker up to 7.0.1. This affects the function LC_WPOffsetValid of the file fsw/src/lc_watch.c of the component Watchpoint Processing. Performing a manipulation results in integer overflow. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been released to the public and may be used for attacks. The pull request to fix this issue awaits acceptance.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Out-of-bounds Read vulnerability. An attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to sensitive information exposure and application instability.
