This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The payload must be encoded as C-style escape sequences (e.g. \x3c/\x3e) at storage time so that wp_kses_post — applied on save for users lacking unfiltered_html — passes it through without stripping angle brackets; WordPress core's shortcode_parse_atts() then decodes the escapes into real HTML characters at render time.

The All-in-One Video Gallery – Video Player & Galleries for YouTube, Vimeo & Self-Hosted Videos plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'embedcode' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.2.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The plugin grants the Subscriber role the edit_aiovg_videos and edit_published_aiovg_videos capabilities on activation, and save_meta_data() accepts the 'embedcode' type without checking current_user_can('unfiltered_html'), meaning any Subscriber can store a malicious shortcode containing a data: URI in the hls attribute that hls.js later processes and Plyr writes into the DOM via innerHTML.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability. A high privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Remote execution.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability. A high privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Remote execution.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains a Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition') vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Denial of service.

n8n before 2.47.6, 2.48.x before 2.48.3, and 3.x before 3.2.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the AWS Bedrock Chat Model and Embeddings AWS Bedrock nodes, where requests to a custom Bedrock runtime endpoint set in an AWS credential bypass n8n's SSRF protection. An authenticated user who can create AWS credentials can point the endpoint at internal or blocked addresses, causing n8n to send requests there and exposing the start of responses in node errors.

ToolJet before 3.21.96-LTS contains a server-side request forgery protection bypass because getSSRFProtectionOptions passes its safe resolver as dnsLookup instead of lookup. Attackers controlling datasource hostnames can use DNS rebinding in REST API, GraphQL, OpenAPI, or OAuth requests to reach blocked private addresses.

Heym before 0.0.154 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the workflow execute endpoint: anonymous workflows run as any signed-in caller, without an access check, using that caller's credentials and global variables. Authenticated attackers can lure signed-in users to a GET execute link for an attacker-owned anonymous workflow, which the SameSite=Lax session cookie authenticates. The attacker then reads the victim's decrypted credentials from the workflow's run history.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in Samba due to insufficient length checks in winbindd_pam_auth_crap.c. When performing NTLM authentication, the client replies to cryptographic challenges back to the server. These replies have variable lengths, and Winbind fails to check the lan manager response length. When Winbind is used for NTLM authentication, a maliciously crafted request can trigger an out-of-bounds read in Winbind, possibly resulting in a crash.

A flaw was found in the exFAT driver of the Linux kernel. The vulnerability exists in the implementation of the file name reconstruction function, which is responsible for reading file name entries from a directory index and merging file name parts belonging to one file into a single long file name. Since the file name characters are copied into a stack variable, a local privileged attacker could use this flaw to overflow the kernel stack.

A flaw was found in the Netfilter subsystem in the Linux kernel. The sctp_mt_check did not validate the flag_count field. This flaw allows a local privileged (CAP_NET_ADMIN) attacker to trigger an out-of-bounds read, leading to a crash or information disclosure.

A flaw was found in KVM. An improper check in svm_set_x2apic_msr_interception() may allow direct access to host x2apic msrs when the guest resets its apic, potentially leading to a denial of service condition.

A vulnerability was found in systemd-resolved. This issue may allow systemd-resolved to accept records of DNSSEC-signed domains even when they have no signature, allowing man-in-the-middles (or the upstream DNS resolver) to manipulate records.
A flaw was found in Booth, a cluster ticket manager. If a specially-crafted hash is passed to gcry_md_get_algo_dlen(), it may allow an invalid HMAC to be accepted by the Booth server.

A security issue was discovered in the LRA Coordinator component of Narayana. When Cancel is called in LRA, an execution time of approximately 2 seconds occurs. If Join is called with the same LRA ID within that timeframe, the application may crash or hang indefinitely, leading to a denial of service.

he Live Auction Cockpit in SAP Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) uses a deprecated java applet component within the affected SRM packages which allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute malicious script in the victim�s browser. This vulnerability has low impact on confidentiality and integrity within the scope of that victim�s browser, with no effect on availability of the application

The Live Auction Cockpit in SAP Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) uses a deprecated java applet component within the affected SRM packages which allows an unauthenticated attacker to craft a malicious link, which when clicked by a victim, redirects the browser to a malicious site. On successful exploitation, the attacker could cause low impact on confidentiality and integrity with no impact on the availability of the application.

A flaw was found in the X Rendering extension's handling of animated cursors. If a client provides no cursors, the server assumes at least one is present, leading to an out-of-bounds read and potential crash.

A flaw exists within the Linux kernel's handling of new TCP connections. The issue results from the lack of memory release after its effective lifetime. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to create a denial of service condition on the system.

Due to a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the SAP Supplier Relationship Management, an unauthenticated attacker could generate a malicious link and make it publicly accessible. If an authenticated victim clicks on the link, the injected input is processed during the page generation, resulting in the execution of malicious content. This execution allows the attacker to access and modify information within the victim's browser scope, impacting confidentiality and integrity, while availability remains unaffected.

A flaw was found in Libsoup. The server-side digest authentication implementation in the SoupAuthDomainDigest class does not properly track issued nonces or enforce the required incrementing nonce-count (nc) attribute. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to capture a single valid authentication header and replay it repeatedly. Consequently, the attacker can bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to protected resources, impersonating the legitimate user.

A flaw was found in GNU Binutils. This heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability, specifically an out-of-bounds read in the bfd linker, allows an attacker to gain access to sensitive information. By convincing a user to process a specially crafted XCOFF object file, an attacker can trigger this flaw, potentially leading to information disclosure or an application level denial of service.

A flaw was found in GNU Binutils. This vulnerability, a heap-based buffer overflow, specifically an out-of-bounds read, exists in the bfd linker component. An attacker could exploit this by convincing a user to process a specially crafted malicious XCOFF object file. Successful exploitation may lead to the disclosure of sensitive information or cause the application to crash, resulting in an application level denial of service.

A vulnerability in the assisted-service REST API, an optional Assisted Installer (assisted-service) component in the Multicluster Engine (MCE), allows an authenticated user with minimal namespace-scoped privileges to obtain administrative credentials for arbitrary clusters provisioned through the hub. 

The credentials download endpoint (GET /v2/clusters/{cluster_id}/credentials, which returns the kubeadmin password) and the kubeconfig download endpoint are operational in AUTH_TYPE=local mode, the only authentication mode available in on-premises ACM/MCE hub deployments. The local authenticator unconditionally grants full administrative access to any request bearing a valid JWT, with no per-endpoint restrictions. A valid local JWT is embedded as a plaintext query parameter in InfraEnvStatus.ISODownloadURL and is readable by any user who has get rights on an InfraEnv object in their own namespace.

The affected components ship as part of Multicluster Engine (MCE). The Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) deployments that include MCE are equally affected.
This issue does not affect the hosted SaaS offering (console.redhat.com), which uses a different authentication mode.

Successful exploitation gives the attacker the kubeadmin password and kubeconfig for any OpenShift cluster provisioned through the affected hub, granting unrestricted root-level administrative access to those spoke clusters.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the XKB geometry processing, specifically within the `CheckSetGeom()` and `XkbAddGeomKeyAlias` functions, allows an attacker to read uninitialized or out-of-bounds memory. An attacker with a connection to the X11 server, either locally or remotely, can exploit this without user interaction. This could lead to the disclosure of memory contents or cause a denial of service by crashing the server.

A flaw was found in the X.Org X server. This vulnerability, an out-of-bounds read, affects the XKB (X Keyboard Extension) modifier map handling. An attacker with access to the X11 server can exploit this by sending a malformed request, which causes the server to read beyond its intended memory boundaries. This can lead to the exposure of sensitive information or cause the server to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in 389 Directory Server. The dereference control plugin does not check for allocation failure before using a BER structure, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to crash the LDAP server when the system is under memory pressure.

A heap buffer over-read vulnerability was discovered in libsoup's (versions: libsoup 3.0 to 3.7.0) HTTP/2 connection tracking framework. When the library processes an HTTP/2 GOAWAY frame, it improperly handles the "Additional Debug Data" payload by assuming the data stream is a safely NUL-terminated C-string. Because the parser lacks strict length-boundary verification before reading this data, a remote, unauthenticated attacker can intentionally send a malformed GOAWAY frame missing the appropriate null delimiter. This causes the library to read past the end of the allocated buffer, triggering an application crash that results in a denial of service (DoS), or potentially exposing fragments of memory contents.

A vulnerability was found in libsoup's HTTP/2 protocol implementation. The library fails to correctly release memory context blocks under specific stream termination conditions, such as when an HTTP/2 connection encounters window exhaustion or explicit stream resets. A remote, unauthenticated attacker acting as a malicious network peer can trick the connection engine into allocating stream states that are subsequently leaked during cleanup. Over a sustained period, this flaw allows the remote attacker to consume the system's heap allocations incrementally, triggering a denial of service (DoS) through an ultimate Out-of-Memory (OOM) application crash.

A flaw was found in Dogtag PKI's ACME responder where the HTTP-01 challenge validator accepts IP address literals as dns identifiers and follows HTTP redirects without validating that the target is a public address. An unauthenticated ACME account holder can exploit this to perform server-side request forgery (SSRF), making the Dogtag server send HTTP GET requests to internal network services. With the InMemory database backend, the response body of internal targets is disclosed to the attacker through the ACME challenge error.

An out-of-bounds read vulnerability was found in swtpm's SWTPM_NVRAM_CheckHeader() function. The entry guard checks the buffer length against sizeof(bh), where bh is a pointer, instead of sizeof(*bh), the actual struct size. This allows an undersized buffer to pass validation, causing a 2-byte heap overread on 64-bit systems (6 bytes on 32-bit) when accessing the totlen field. This may cause daemon termination on some platforms and leaks heap data to the log.

A flaw was found in the file-pix (ESM) plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted PIX image file, the plugin allocates a Variable-Length Array (VLA) on the stack without proper bounds checking, causing an unbounded stack allocation followed by a 21-byte stack over-read. This can result in a denial of service due to stack exhaustion and a limited information disclosure of stack memory contents into an intermediate file.

A flaw was found in CRI-O's container-creation environment-variable handling
(`mergeEnvs` in `server/utils.go`, consumed by `setupContainerEnvironmentAndWorkdir` in
`server/container_create.go`). When a `CreateContainer` request supplies a `nil` CRI
`Envs` field, CRI-O falls back to using the target OCI image's `config.Env` entries
unfiltered, in contrast to the normal merge path, which validates each entry for a
`key=value` form before use. An OCI image whose `config.Env` contains an entry with no
`=` character (e.g. a bare `NOEQUALS` string) causes CRI-O to split that entry into a
single-element slice and then index its second element, which is out of range. This
triggers an unrecovered Go runtime panic in the `crio` daemon process, crashing it and
terminating the container-runtime service for all workloads on the node until it is
restarted.

A flaw was found in jwcrypto. A remote attacker can send a specially crafted JSON Web Encryption (JWE) token containing numerous period delimiters. This malformed token can force the JWE.deserialize() function to allocate excessive memory, leading to a MemoryError. This issue results in a denial of service (DoS) for services that process untrusted JWE values.

A flaw was found in gdk-pixbuf. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a heap out-of-bounds read by providing a specially crafted Apple Icon Image (.icns) file. The uncompress() function, which handles RLE-encoded ICNS icon data, fails to validate the source buffer's boundaries during decompression. This can lead to a denial of service, where the application crashes, or to information disclosure, potentially revealing sensitive data from adjacent memory.

An integer overflow in BSON value-length handling in the MongoDB Go Driver can cause a runtime panic when an application validates or accesses a malformed BSON document. An unauthenticated actor who can supply BSON bytes to an affected application may terminate an unprotected application process, causing a denial of service. The driver's server-monitoring path contains panic recovery and is limited to server-selection failure.

Improper validation of a BSON array length in the MongoDB Go Driver can cause an out-of-bounds index and runtime panic when an application calls bson.RawArray.Validate or bsoncore.Array.Validate on a malformed four-byte array. An unauthenticated actor who can supply raw BSON array data to an affected application may terminate an unprotected application process, causing a denial of service. No confidentiality or integrity impact has been identified.

A flaw was found in gnome-remote-desktop as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. In the VNC TLS read path, partial consumption of the internal peek buffer incorrectly moves remaining peeked bytes into the caller-supplied buffer instead of compacting the peek buffer. A remote attacker who can reach an enabled VNC TLS listener and trigger a peek/read size mismatch can cause an out-of-bounds write, leading to denial of service.

A flaw was found in luksmeta. Improper boundary validation of metadata slots allows an attacker capable of supplying or modifying a disk header to redirect wipe or load operations outside the intended metadata area. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by providing a crafted header with valid checksums to overwrite or zero out encrypted payload data, resulting in persistent data loss and corrupted storage. Exploitation typically requires privileged access to modify raw block devices or the ability to induce an administrator to process an untrusted disk image.

A flaw was found in GIMP. An attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) or potentially disclose sensitive memory contents by convincing a user to open or preview a specially crafted Bohemia Interactive (PAA) texture file. Due to an integer overflow when calculating image dimensions during file decompression, the application allocates an undersized memory buffer. Subsequent processing reads memory past the buffer boundary, terminating the plug-in process unexpectedly.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Email Center product of Oracle E-Business Suite (component: Message Component).  Supported versions that are affected are 12.2.3-12.2.15. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Email Center.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Email Center, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Email Center accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Email Center accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 6.1 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N).

A flaw was found in Ghostscript. When processing a specially crafted TrueType font or document embedding one, an accounting error during font rendering can bypass buffer size checks, triggering a heap-based buffer overflow. A remote attacker could exploit this by enticing a victim or automated service to open the malicious content, potentially resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) crash or arbitrary code execution.

A flaw was found in the libstdc++ component of GCC. An attacker who can provide an excessively large element count to a boolean vector (std::vector<bool>) constructor can trigger an integer wrap during internal memory calculations. This issue leaves the container in an inconsistent state, leading to out-of-bounds memory access and resulting in an application crash or a Denial of Service (DoS) during subsequent operations.

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the Nikon metadata tag parser, a pointer can be dereferenced without verifying that data remains in the buffer, causing out-of-bounds reads. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

A flaw was found in GStreamer gst-plugins-good (avidemux). In the superindex and subindex parsers, integer overflow can bypass bounds checks and cause out-of-bounds reads. Because avidemux is auto-plugged by playbin, decodebin, and gst-discoverer, opening or previewing a crafted AVI is sufficient to trigger the issue. Fixed upstream in gst-plugins-good 1.28.6 (GStreamer-SA-2026-0072).

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the Musepack SV7 decoder because mpc7_decode_init() does not validate lastframelen against MPC_FRAME_SIZE. Attackers can supply a crafted Musepack SV7 file declaring an oversized final frame, causing consumers of decoded frames to read past the audio buffer, leading to crashes or heap memory disclosure.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in bitpacked_decode_uyvy422() in libavcodec/bitpacked_dec.c because it never verifies packets hold width * height * 2 bytes. Attackers can supply truncated bitpacked UYVY422 packets via crafted SDP/RFC 4175 RTP sessions or raw input to crash applications or expose adjacent heap memory.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an integer underflow in decode_frame() in libavcodec/lcldec.c that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read via short ZLIB packets with FLAG_MULTITHREAD. Attackers can supply a crafted AVI or MKV file with an LCL video stream whose packet is shorter than 8 bytes, bypassing length clamping to crash the decoding application.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the SGI encoder's encode_frame() in libavcodec/sgienc.c, where unsigned size variables mis-handle negative linesize frames. Attackers can supply a video whose display matrix triggers autorotate vflip, so transcoding to SGI images reads pixel data far outside the frame and crashes the process.

A flaw was found in OpenSCAP. A heap-based buffer overflow can occur when processing a specially crafted Extensible Configuration Checklist Description Format (XCCDF) document using the sds-compose option. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to corrupt memory, resulting in an application crash and a Denial of Service (DoS).
Use after free in Windows Hyper-V allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs by manipulating the objUrl parameter in Ctrl.php's redir() function. Attackers can craft login links with objUrl set to a malicious site, causing the application to issue an HTTP 302 redirect to that external URL, which can be abused for phishing and credential theft.

Omnispace Agora Project before 26.11.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows attackers to inject malicious HTML markup by controlling imported directory data or an uploaded CSV file, as values are rendered into table cell text and value attributes after only Txt::utf8Encode() with no HTML escaping in VuePersonsImportExport.php. Attackers can craft a CSV cell containing an attribute-breakout payload that is rendered verbatim and executed in the browser of the administrator performing the import, leading to arbitrary script execution in the administrative context.

Issue summary: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX
may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end
of the caller-supplied output buffer.

Impact summary: No path by which an attacker can trigger this has been
identified. An application that passes an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock() could suffer a heap buffer overflow, crashing or corrupting
its own memory, but it must itself supply such a length.

CWE: CWE-190: Integer Overflow or Wraparound

Description: EVP_EncodeBlock() base64-encodes a buffer of a caller-supplied
length into an output buffer that the caller allocates. The caller is expected
to reserve 4*((len+2)/3)+1 bytes. For input lengths close to INT_MAX, the
arithmetic that computes the encoded length overflows a signed integer, so the
function writes more data than the documented output size. The result is a
heap buffer overflow in the calling process.

Reaching this requires an application to pass an input length near INT_MAX to
EVP_EncodeBlock(). OpenSSL's TLS, QUIC and CMS implementations never encode
buffers of that size, and the command line tools cannot practically be made to
do so: the limits on reading a proxy password from a file and on bignum sizes
prevent it. An application that accepts an attacker-controlled length and
forwards it to EVP_EncodeBlock() without its own bound check is exposed.

The severity is Low because no attacker-controlled path to the overflow is
known. The caller must already hold a buffer of about two gigabytes before the
defect can be reached.

FIPS impact: no
The affected code is outside the FIPS module boundary.

lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap() in src/ext4_fs.c because it does not validate s_inodes_per_group against the inode bitmap size. Attackers can supply a crafted ext4 image with an oversized s_inodes_per_group so memset writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing the mounting application.

Dell Enterprise Sonic Distribution, versions prior to 4.6.1, contains a Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to a Denial of service.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains a stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability in ff_h264_parse_framesize() in libavformat/rtpdec_h264.c when parsing an SDP a=framesize attribute lacking a height. Attackers controlling an RTSP server DESCRIBE response or a crafted .sdp file can make atoi() read past the line buffer, crashing clients or parsing stale stack bytes.

FFmpeg before 9.1 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the split_planes size check of write_packet() in libavformat/img2enc.c that allows out-of-bounds heap reads. Attackers can supply a crafted input whose rawvideo stream declares very large width and height, remuxed into .y image files, to leak heap memory into output files or crash the application.
The log viewer of Zoraxy admin panel fails to neutralize the output properly, that may cause an arbitrary script to be executed on the administrator's browser.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Apache Allura's ticket tracking tool.



This issue affects Apache Allura: before 1.23.0.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 1.23.0, which fixes the issue.

hping3 through commit 3547c76 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in display_ipopt() that allows remote attackers to overflow the static 40-byte old_rr buffer via a crafted IP Record Route option. Attackers acting as the probed host, on-path, or spoofing the target can send replies with option lengths up to 255 to hping3 running with -G/--rroute, corrupting global memory and crashing hping3.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the glTF 1.0 importer that allows attackers to read adjacent heap memory by supplying an unchecked KHR_binary_glTF image bufferView. Attackers can craft a glTF or GLB file whose bufferView byteOffset or byteLength exceeds its buffer, disclosing heap memory through embedded texture data or crashing the process.

browser-use before 1.0.0 contains a URL parser differential vulnerability in SecurityWatchdog that allows attackers to bypass allowed_domains, prohibited_domains, and block_ip_addresses checks by crafting a URL with a backslash before the allowed host, exploiting the mismatch between urllib.parse hostname extraction and Chromium's WHATWG-style URL parsing. Attackers can influence an LLM-controlled navigate action, such as through prompt injection, to send requests to loopback or private addresses or arbitrary external hosts before the browser redirects to about:blank, enabling SSRF and persistent state changes on the target server.

GNU Inetutils talkd Stack-based Buffer Overflow Denial-of-Service Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to create a denial-of-service condition on affected installations of GNU Inetutils. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.

The specific flaw exists within the processing of announce requests. The issue results from the lack of proper validation of the length of user-supplied data prior to copying it to a fixed-length stack-based buffer. An attacker can leverage this vulnerability to create a denial-of-service condition on the system. Was ZDI-CAN-29120.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Enterprise Linux's qemu-kvm virtualization software. A privileged user inside a guest virtual machine could use this flaw to make the host QEMU process copy parts of its own memory into the guest's memory, where the attacker could read it. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to view portions of the host QEMU process memory from within a guest, potentially exposing sensitive information that could aid in further attacks. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in mailboxes/detach.cgi that allows unauthenticated mail senders to bypass the HTML sanitizer. Attackers can send HTML attachments with entity-obfuscated javascript: schemes or encoded script tags in iframe srcdoc to execute script in the Webmin session of users opening them.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts by submitting malicious failed-login usernames. Attackers can repeatedly submit crafted usernames until blocked, executing script in administrator sessions viewing edit_blocked.cgi in Webmin or Usermin.

Webmin through 2.670 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in postfix/view_mailq.cgi and sendmail/view_mailq.cgi that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via unsanitized MIME attachment filenames. Attackers can send a message with a crafted Content-Disposition or Content-Type filename that remains queued, executing script in the Webmin session of users viewing it.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that allows man-in-the-middle attackers to capture credentials because servers/save_serv.cgi skips the selected SSL certificate check. When fast RPC is set to Automatic, attackers intercepting the /fastrpc.cgi probe can obtain the remote Webmin username and password sent via HTTP Basic Authorization.

Webmin through 2.670 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in servers/link.cgi that accepts self-signed certificates for linked servers even when certificate checking is enabled. Man-in-the-middle attackers presenting a self-signed certificate with the correct hostname can capture stored HTTP Basic credentials for the remote Webmin and inject HTML into the local Webmin origin.

A flaw was found in rsyslog. When using the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) output module (omdtls) configured to authenticate receivers by name or fingerprint, the module validates the certificate chain against trusted certificate authorities but fails to verify that the certificate matches the intended receiver's identity or fingerprint. An attacker who can redirect or intercept outbound network traffic and present a certificate issued by a trusted certificate authority could capture forwarded log data, leading to information disclosure.

The Web To Print Shop : uDraw WordPress plugin through 3.4.0 does not validate URLs taken from the request before fetching them server-side and returning the response, allowing unauthenticated users to make the server request internal resources and read the responses.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Argument Injection vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to disclosure of sensitive information and limited integrity impact.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in 2.10 Legacy Theming in Apache JSPWIKI version 2.10.0 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows specially crafted filenames of uploaded attachments to potentially render unescaped html or javascript to the browser.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in the Markdown renderer of Apache JSPWiki 2.11.0 through 3.0.0 on all platforms, when the Markdown syntax is enabled, allows an attacker who can edit a page to execute javascript in the browser of a visitor of that page. The text and the url of an inline image were written into the attributes of the img element without encoding.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue. A fix was also backported to 2.12.6

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in ListLocksPlugin in Apache JSPWiki 2.10.2 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows an attacker to execute javascript in the browser of a visitor of a page that uses the plugin. 




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

A Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability reflected in the usuario[nombre] parameter of the actualizar_cuenta function in the functions.php endpoint. The application does not properly sanitise the received content, meaning that an authenticated user can inject JavaScript code which is reflected in the web interface and in the JSON responses. If another user views the affected content, the code may be executed within the context of their browser.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Apache JSPWiki.



This issue affects Apache JSPWiki: through 2.12.4.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.12.5, which fixes the issue.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in Group.jsp in Apache JSPWIKI on versions older than 2.12.5 allows attacker to execute javascript via a specially crafted url
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.12.5, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting (XSS) in JSPWIKI in versions 2.12.4 and older. allows attacker to execute javascript via injection using the image plugin.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.12.5, which fixes this issue.

Injection/Cross Site Scripting potential in SvnStyleDiffProvider in Apache JSPWIKI 3.0.0 on all platforms allows improperly formatted content to render within the browser, potentially exposing javascript based exploits. 
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting/Injection in Apache JSPWIKI versions 2.X to 3.0.0 inclusive on all platforms allows an attacker to potentially render unescaped inputs to the browser when creating a new page.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site scripting/injection in ReferringUndefinedPagesPlugin in Apache JSPWIKI on all platforms allows specific fields in the plugin to render unescaped content to the browser.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1 which fixes this issue.

Stored XSS/Cross Site Scripting/Injection in the attachment servlet in Apache JSPWIKI on all platforms, all previous versions allows an attacker to upload a malicious HTML file and then potentially have it rendered in browser due to lax rules of rendering inline vs a file download.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting/injection in WeblogPlugin in Apache JSPWIKI on all versions previous to 3.0.1 on all platforms allows an attack to bypass content encodingf mechanisms to render raw html or javascript onto the page.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site scripting/injection in SampleAjaxPlugin in Apache JSPWIKI on all versions prior to 3.0.1 on all platforms allows attacker to bypass page encoding, potentially rendering raw html or javascript on the page

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting in Markdown renderer in Apache JSPWIKI 2.4 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows attacker to bypass html encoding techniques to potentially render raw html or javascript in the browser.
Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Cross Site Scripting/Injection in PageTab.jsp in Apache JSPWIKI versions 2.10 through 3.0.0 on all platforms allows an attacker to make a specially crafted wiki page and share a custom URL that bypasses html and javascript encoding techniques, enabling render and execution in the browser.




Users are recommended to upgrade to version 3.0.1, which fixes this issue.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway (SCG) Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Argument Injection vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to disclosure of sensitive information and limited integrity impact.

POCO C++ Libraries through 1.15.4 contain a denial of service vulnerability in InflatingStreamBuf::reset() and InflatingInputStream::reset() that fails to discard unconsumed compressed input after decompression errors. Attackers can supply one corrupt zlib, gzip or zip-deflate stream to applications reusing an InflatingInputStream, causing all later stream reads, including valid ones, to fail.

libyang through 6.4.13 contains a release of invalid pointer vulnerability in ly_in_memory() and ly_in_memory_chunk() in src/in.c that return the current read position instead of the previous start address. Attackers supplying YANG data parsed from a heap buffer can cause applications freeing the returned pointer to pass an interior address to free(), aborting the process.

POCO C++ Libraries through 1.15.4 contain a denial of service vulnerability in InflatingStreamBuf::reset() that fails to clear stale buffered data from a previous failed stream. Attackers can supply one corrupt compressed stream to an application reusing an InflatingOutputStream, causing subsequent valid streams to fail decompression.

Boost.JSON 1.75.0 through 1.92.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in monotonic_resource::release() because it does not reset next_size_ when returning blocks upstream. Attackers can send repeated JSON documents larger than the initial block, growing allocation sizes geometrically until every later allocation fails with bad_alloc.

HortusFox through 6.4 contains an information exposure vulnerability in BackupModule::start that allows unauthenticated attackers to download workspace backups stored in the public/backup directory. Attackers can enumerate one-second-precision creation timestamps used as filenames to retrieve archives containing locations, plants, gallery, tasks, inventory and calendar data.

Part-DB (Part-DB-server) before 2.20.6 contains an open redirect vulnerability in several controllers that pass user-supplied _redirect or redirect_back parameters to redirect() without validating local paths. Attackers can craft links to endpoints like /tools/batch_eda_edit using scheme-relative or protocol-relative values that bypass the nelmio_security guard, sending authenticated victims to attacker-controlled phishing sites.

A NULL pointer dereference and invalid memory release in the server discovery component of the MongoDB C Driver may allow an unauthenticated party that controls a server endpoint, or that can alter unencrypted network traffic, to cause a client application to terminate by sending a crafted discovery response.

ToolJet from 3.16.0 before 3.20.256 contains an improper signature verification vulnerability in StripeWebhookGuard that validates webhooks against a self-generated signature instead of the Stripe-Signature header. Unauthenticated attackers can post forged Stripe events to the POST /api/organization/payment/webhooks route to activate subscriptions, generate licenses, change plans or seats, and add AI credits without payment.

GNOME libxml2 through 2.15.4 contains a double free vulnerability in xmlReaderNewWalker() that frees reader->input again after xmlTextReaderClose() already released it. Applications reusing a closed xmlTextReader with xmlReaderNewWalker() can crash, and groomed heap memory can control the close callback for possible code execution.

libvorbis through 1.3.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in _ov_getlap() in lib/vorbisfile.c that passes a negative sample count from vorbis_synthesis_lapout() to memcpy(). Attackers can supply a short, valid Ogg Vorbis file with suitable block sizes to overwrite stack frames and crash applications performing two consecutive lapped seeks.

diaspora* through 0.10.1, using the diaspora_federation gem through 1.2.0, contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to make the pod send requests to arbitrary internal hosts by supplying a crafted diaspora handle to the GET /link endpoint, which triggers WebFinger discovery without private-address filtering. Attackers can specify a handle containing an IPv4/IPv6 address and port such as diaspora://probe@host:port to force the HttpClient to connect to loopback, RFC1918, link-local, or cloud metadata addresses, enabling blind probing of the pod's internal network.

Faveo Helpdesk (Community) through 2.0.3 and 2.0.4.RC.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in ApiExceptAuthController::checkUrl(), reachable through the unauthenticated and unthrottled GET /api/v1/helpdesk/url route, which validates the url parameter only as a well-formed URL, appends the fixed path api/v1/helpdesk/check-url and fetches it with curl with TLS certificate verification disabled and no restriction on the target host, port or address range. Unauthenticated attackers can choose the scheme, host and port of the request to make the server connect to internal hosts and services, including loopback and private addresses, and read the response body, which is returned in the JSON result field.

psqlODBC read memory it had not written, or memory past the end of an application buffer, and sent it to the server or returned it to the application:

- Text bound as SQL_C_CHAR to a large-object parameter was read past the end of the application's buffer, and the extra bytes were stored in the large object.
- After a fetch truncated a long bytea or large-object value, positioned updates and inserts read past the bound buffer and wrote that memory into the row.
- Hex text with a NUL byte, bound to a binary parameter with an explicit length, sent uninitialised heap memory as the parameter value.
- With RowVersioning=1, SQLColumns() on a table that does not exist returned uninitialised stack memory as the schema and table names.
- With UseDeclareFetch=1, bookmarks of updatable block cursors contained uninitialised heap memory, and a malformed ctid from the server sent stale heap bytes in positioned updates and deletes.
- With UseServerSidePrepare=0, calling SQLNumResultCols(), SQLDescribeCol() or SQLColAttribute() on a prepared statement before SQLExecute() read the application's bound parameter buffers and sent their current contents to the server as literals, although ODBC lets the application fill those buffers after the describe.
- The driver named the prepared statements, savepoints, cursors and keyset plans it creates on the server after the heap addresses of its own objects, so the server, or anyone reading an unencrypted connection, learned exact heap addresses inside the client.

Depending on the case, an end user who supplies a parameter value, a database user who stores a long value in a row, or a hostile server can obtain memory of the application process, which may hold data of other users or credentials.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to conduct a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack against a user of the interface. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary script code in a victim's browser in the context of the web interface.

In Revive Adserver through 6.0.9, unauthenticated request parameters in ad delivery can cause reflected cross-site scripting. A crafted delivery URL places a macro token in the source or target parameter and malicious markup in the referer parameter. Macro replacement after initial input encoding can insert the unescaped markup into generated banner output, causing JavaScript execution in the delivery origin when a visitor follows the URL. An active banner is required.

A flaw was found in bootc. On a sealed composefs boot with a strict composefs digest on the kernel command line, the initramfs derives fs-verity enforcement from unsigned repository metadata and can mount an image under images/refs without measuring it against that digest. An attacker with offline write access to the root filesystem can boot a modified root under a legitimately signed UKI.

Pydantic AI Harness's PlaywrightBrowser applies an egress policy to the requests a page makes. It treated any URL containing a backslash as having no host, and it allows script and asset requests with no host. A page script could therefore add a backslash to a URL's query to send requests to private addresses, to hosts outside allowed_domains, and to hosts in blocked_domains.

This affects applications that use PlaywrightBrowser to open pages or follow instructions an attacker can influence. It applies to fetch, XHR, sendBeacon, WebSocket and passive asset requests. Navigation and frames were not affected. A policy that limits every request kind to an allowlist did not prevent data from being sent to another host.

Responses from private services could be read only when the service permits cross-origin reads or accepts the WebSocket connection. Current Chromium versions separately block many requests from public pages to private addresses, but not requests between public hosts, and not when the browser runs behind a forward proxy.

The assumed attacker is a third party with no access to the application who controls script on a page the agent opens, or content that steers the agent's browser tools.

Upgrade pydantic-ai-harness to 0.74.0 or later. Until then, enforce egress outside the browser with a firewall or a filtering proxy, and do not rely on the browser's domain lists for untrusted pages.

The Broken Link Notifier plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'content_links[] / header_links[] / footer_links[]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.0.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The script executes in the administrator's wp-admin session only when the administrator clicks the Replace Link action on the injected row, meaning successful exploitation requires tricking an administrator into performing that action. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Calculated Fields Form – AI Form Builder for WordPress – Contact, Payment, Quote, Quiz & More plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'x' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.6.0.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Exploitation requires the WordPress site to have a published form configured with a URL-backed text field (using the predefined url.x attribute) wired through a calculated-field equation that calls set_timeslots(); without this non-default form configuration, the vulnerable sink is unreachable.

The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'textarea-1' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.58.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution is not automatic on page load; the injected script runs only when an administrator actively clicks the stored ThickBox link, at which point WordPress ThickBox JS decodes the entity-encoded title attribute and writes it into #TB_ajaxWindowTitle via innerHTML in the administrator's origin. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

openFrameworks through 0.12.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the ofxAndroid OFZipUtil.extract helper that allows attackers to write files outside the extraction directory. Attackers can supply a crafted ZIP archive with entries like ../escaped.txt to write or overwrite files with the Android application's file permissions.

Juspay Hyperswitch 1.8.0 before 1.129.0 uses a hardcoded default webhook secret that allows unauthenticated attackers to forge Stripe webhooks when no merchant webhook secret is configured. Attackers knowing a merchant ID and connector transaction ID can sign a crafted payment_intent.succeeded event with "default_secret" to mark uncaptured payments as succeeded.

The VK Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.130.0 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the moderator to interact with the inline Reply action on the edit-comments screen, which is a routine action triggered when a moderation-held comment is reviewed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.54 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Execution of the injected script requires an administrator to use the plugin's own "Add 301 Redirect" workflow on the attacker's logged 404 row, which causes the entity-laundered double quote to be written into the redirects table and subsequently rendered unescaped in the administrator's browser. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Postie plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 1.9.89 via the 'postie' parameter. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract the plaintext POP3/IMAP mailbox password and username, SMTP configuration, absolute server filesystem paths, and all SQL queries executed during the mail-fetch run from the debug response body. Exploitation requires the site administrator to have enabled the 'Enable Debug Logging' (postie_log_debug) option, which is off by default but is routinely toggled on during troubleshooting and left enabled.

The WP Go Maps – Google Map, OpenStreetMap, Leaflet & Store Locator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'query' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 10.2.05 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Exploitation requires that the site administrator has enabled the plugin's 'Enable Dynamic SQL Refactors' setting and that the database server is running with a sql_mode containing NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES; neither condition is enabled by default.

Parse Server before 9.12.0-alpha.2 matches $in, $nin, $all and $containedBy constraints in LiveQuery with a cost proportional to the product of the constraint list size and the saved array size. A client that can subscribe to a class and save objects in it can use large lists and arrays to block the event loop for seconds or longer, stalling LiveQuery and, when it runs in the same process, Parse Server.

Coder 2.29.17 before 2.29.27, 2.32.7 before 2.33.0, 2.33.8 before 2.34.0, 2.34.2 before 2.34.19, 2.35.0 before 2.37.11, 2.38.0 before 2.38.7, and 2.39.0 before 2.39.1 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows malicious template authors to steal session tokens because coder open app substitutes $SESSION_TOKEN into template-defined external app URLs without validating scheme or destination. Attackers can define an external app URL or IDE link pointing to an attacker server so users running coder open app leak their token, enabling impersonation of shared users or administrators.

Frappe Framework before 15.120.0 and 16.x before 16.33.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the handling of the X-Frappe-Request-Id HTTP header when monitoring is enabled. Remote unauthenticated attackers can send crafted header values to infer database contents through blind SQL injection techniques.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allow CPU exhaustion because, on PHP without GMP, AbstractECDH falls back to pure PHP curve code that converts unbounded ECDH-ES epk x and y coordinates to big integers before any length check. Unauthenticated attackers who know only the recipient key's curve can send small JWEs with oversized epk coordinates, keeping workers busy for seconds to minutes per token.

Web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 contain a denial of service vulnerability in RSAKey, which accepts RSA keys with a modulus and public exponent of unbounded length. Remote attackers can supply a crafted key, such as in the jwk header of a DPoP proof, to force seconds of CPU per PS256/PS384/PS512 verification or RSA encryption, or per any RSA operation when GMP is unavailable.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 (and jwt-encryption through 3.2.10) do not check the key length in JWEBuilder and JWEDecrypter for direct (dir) encryption, so undersized keys are zero-padded. Anyone holding a token issued with a half-size AES-CBC-HMAC key can decrypt it, and an empty key also allows forging tokens the decrypter accepts.

Web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6, and jwt-core through 3.2.10, perform unblinded RSA private key operations in RSAKey::exponentiate(), so CRT recombination time reveals whether a decrypted RSA-OAEP, RSA-OAEP-256, or RSA1_5 value is below the prime q. Attackers who can submit JWEs can time rejections of crafted tokens to binary search q, factor the modulus, and decrypt all JWEs encrypted to that key.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 parse JSON General serialized JWS tokens in quadratic time because JSONGeneralSerializer::unserialize() adds each signature via JWS::addSignature(), which clones the token. Unauthenticated remote attackers can send large tokens holding thousands of empty signatures to exhaust CPU and occupy PHP workers without any valid key or token.

web-token jwt-framework and jwt-library before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6, and jwt-encryption and jwt-signature through 3.2.10, contain a denial of service vulnerability because the JWS and JWE serializers pass attacker-controlled tokens and protected headers to json_decode() without bounds before verification. Unauthenticated attackers can submit large tokens with colliding header member names or deeply nested arrays to cause quadratic decoding time or fatal memory exhaustion.

web-token jwt-framework before 3.4.13, 4.0.x before 4.0.9, 4.1.x before 4.1.11, and 4.2.x before 4.2.6 allows denial of service because JWELoader and JWSLoader try every recipient or signature of a JSON General serialized token without limiting their number. Unauthenticated attackers can send a small JWE with many empty recipients inheriting a maximal PBES2 p2c value, forcing repeated key derivations that exhaust worker CPU.

The LiteSpeed Cache plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'REQUEST_URI' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.9.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires comments to be open, a comment author name containing a literal quotation mark stored via WordPress's ENT_NOQUOTES save pipeline, a raw HTTP client capable of sending unencoded " and > characters in the request path, and — under default WordPress moderation — prior moderator approval of the crafted comment.

The Export Products, Orders & Customers for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'start_date' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.4.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. Successful exploitation requires the victim — who must hold the manage_woocommerce capability (administrator or shop manager) — to both open the attacker-crafted URL and click the start_date input field on the Export Tools page, as the injected payload is delivered via an onclick handler rather than a page-load event. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

The Easy Social Share Buttons for WordPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 'design' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 11.6 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. The vulnerable endpoint is reached via the ?subscribe-preview=true query parameter, which is processed on template_redirect with no capability or nonce check, making it accessible to unauthenticated users.

A flaw was found in CRI-O. An attacker with access to the kubelet or CRI-O socket can exploit a path traversal vulnerability in the checkpoint restore functionality. This allows the attacker to delete arbitrary files and directories on the host filesystem during a checkpoint restore operation. The vulnerability arises because the system processes entries from checkpoint archive metadata without validating that the files are confined to the container's root directory.

The access rules of JTL-Shop (export/.htaccess and export/backup/.htaccess) release files with the extensions gz and zip for the export directory without withdrawing this release in the subdirectory export/backup, in which the shop stores database dumps and file backups. As a result, backup files in this directory can be downloaded without authentication by anyone who knows or guesses the file name. Up to version 5.5.5 the names of database backups consist only of a timestamp; from version 5.6.0 they contain a random component, which does not replace access control. The backups contain the complete shop database (customer data, orders, password hashes) and, for file backups, files of the shop. The access rules are only evaluated by Apache. On installations where another web server, for example nginx, delivers static files such as gz and zip directly (including nginx in front of Apache), the files remain accessible even with the corrected rules, unless the directory is blocked at server level.

PDFio before 1.6.5 contains an integer underflow in _pdfioCryptoAESDecrypt() in pdfio-aes.c, which strips PKCS#7 padding before any AES block has been decrypted when an AES-encrypted string or binary value holds only its 16-byte IV. Attackers can supply a crafted AES-encrypted PDF that, when opened with pdfioFileOpen(), makes the decrypted length underflow so that _pdfioValueDecrypt() reads and writes out of bounds, crashing the application or corrupting heap memory.

Roundcube Webmail before 1.6.19 and 1.7.x before 1.7.4 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability in compose_part_body() in program/actions/mail/compose.php, which converts a text/enriched message part to HTML for the HTML editor without sanitizing the result. Attackers can send a crafted email with a text/enriched part so that script injected into the HTML editor runs in the victim's session when the victim replies to, forwards, or edits the message.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an External Control of File Name or Path vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Unauthorized access.

Dell Secure Connect Gateway - Virtual Edition, versions prior to 5.36.00.16, contains an Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability. A low privileged local attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Information exposure.

FOG Project before 1.6.0.119 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain host tokens from status/hostgetkey.php by supplying a host MAC address. Attackers can present the token to service/hostinfo.php to retrieve decrypted Active Directory join credentials and Windows product keys during deployment windows.

mcp-video-analyzer 0.2.0 before 0.10.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows attackers to reach internal addresses by supplying any http(s) URL ending in a video extension. Attackers can use prompt injection to make tools like get_frames fetch loopback, private, or cloud metadata addresses directly or via redirects, writing responses to disk or returning rendered screenshots.

A flaw was found in JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) and EC2 Amazon Machine Image (AMI). Incorrect permissions (755) for the /var/cache/jboss-ec2-eap/ directory allow a local user to read sensitive files. This vulnerability can lead to information disclosure, specifically exposing Amazon Web Services (AWS) credentials.
In Apache Airflow before 1.10.2, a malicious admin user could edit the state of objects in the Airflow metadata database to execute arbitrary javascript on certain page views.

An issue was found in Apache Airflow versions 1.10.10 and below. It was discovered that many of the admin management screens in the new/RBAC UI handled escaping incorrectly, allowing authenticated users with appropriate permissions to create stored XSS attacks.
In Apache Airflow versions prior to 1.10.13, the Charts and Query View of the old (Flask-admin based) UI were vulnerable for SSRF attack.

The lineage endpoint of the deprecated Experimental API was not protected by authentication in Airflow 2.0.0. This allowed unauthenticated users to hit that endpoint. This is low-severity issue as the attacker needs to be aware of certain parameters to pass to that endpoint and even after can just get some metadata about a DAG and a Task. This issue affects Apache Airflow 2.0.0.

If remote logging is not used, the worker (in the case of CeleryExecutor) or the scheduler (in the case of LocalExecutor) runs a Flask logging server and is listening on a specific port and also binds on 0.0.0.0 by default. This logging server had no authentication and allows reading log files of DAG jobs. This issue affects Apache Airflow < 2.1.2.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection') vulnerability in Apache Airflow Spark Provider, Apache Airflow allows an attacker to read arbtrary files in the task execution context, without write access to DAG files. This issue affects Spark Provider versions prior to 4.0.0. It also impacts any Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.3.0 in case Spark Provider is installed (Spark Provider 4.0.0 can only be installed for Airflow 2.3.0+). Note that you need to manually install the Spark Provider version 4.0.0 in order to get rid of the vulnerability on top of Airflow 2.3.0+ version that has lower version of the Spark Provider installed).

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel’s IP framework for transforming packets (XFRM subsystem). This issue may allow a malicious user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to directly dereference a NULL pointer in xfrm_update_ae_params(), leading to a possible kernel crash and denial of service.

A buffer overflow flaw was found in base/gdevdevn.c:1973 in devn_pcx_write_rle() in ghostscript. This issue may allow a local attacker to cause a denial of service via outputting a crafted PDF file for a DEVN device with gs.

An integer overflow flaw was found in pcl/pl/plfont.c:418 in pl_glyph_name in ghostscript. This issue may allow a local attacker to cause a denial of service via transforming a crafted PCL file to PDF format.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the siano smsusb module in the Linux kernel. The bug occurs during device initialization when the siano device is plugged in. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system, causing a denial of service condition.

A use-after-free vulnerability was found in the cxgb4 driver in the Linux kernel. The bug occurs when the cxgb4 device is detaching due to a possible rearming of the flower_stats_timer from the work queue. This flaw allows a local user to crash the system, causing a denial of service condition.

A flaw was found in the Linux kernel's TUN/TAP functionality. This issue could allow a local user to bypass network filters and gain unauthorized access to some resources. The original patches fixing CVE-2023-1076 are incorrect or incomplete. The problem is that the following upstream commits - a096ccca6e50 ("tun: tun_chr_open(): correctly initialize socket uid"), - 66b2c338adce ("tap: tap_open(): correctly initialize socket uid"), pass "inode->i_uid" to sock_init_data_uid() as the last parameter and that turns out to not be accurate.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in dbFree in fs/jfs/jfs_dmap.c in the journaling file system (JFS) in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker to crash the system due to a missing sanity check.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in vmxnet3_rq_cleanup in drivers/net/vmxnet3/vmxnet3_drv.c in the networking sub-component in vmxnet3 in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with normal user privilege to cause a denial of service due to a missing sanity check during cleanup.

A memory leak flaw was found in Libtiff's tiffcrop utility. This issue occurs when tiffcrop operates on a TIFF image file, allowing an attacker to pass a crafted TIFF image file to tiffcrop utility, which causes this memory leak issue, resulting an application crash, eventually leading to a denial of service.

A NULL pointer dereference flaw was found in the Linux kernel ipv4 stack. The socket buffer (skb) was assumed to be associated with a device before calling __ip_options_compile, which is not always the case if the skb is re-routed by ipvs. This issue may allow a local user with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to crash the system.

A null pointer dereference vulnerability was found in nft_dynset_init() in net/netfilter/nft_dynset.c in nf_tables in the Linux kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN user privilege to trigger a denial of service.

A null pointer dereference vulnerability was found in dpll_pin_parent_pin_set() in drivers/dpll/dpll_netlink.c in the Digital Phase Locked Loop (DPLL) subsystem in the  Linux kernel. This issue could be exploited to trigger a denial of service.

A memory leak problem was found in ctnetlink_create_conntrack in net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_netlink.c in the Linux Kernel. This issue may allow a local attacker with CAP_NET_ADMIN privileges to cause a denial of service (DoS) attack due to a refcount overflow.

A flaw was found in the blkgs destruction path in block/blk-cgroup.c in the Linux kernel, leading to a cgroup blkio memory leakage problem. When a cgroup is being destroyed, cgroup_rstat_flush() is only called at css_release_work_fn(), which is called when the blkcg reference count reaches 0. This circular dependency will prevent blkcg and some blkgs from being freed after they are made offline. This issue may allow an attacker with a local access to cause system instability, such as an out of memory error.

A denial of service vulnerability due to a deadlock was found in sctp_auto_asconf_init in net/sctp/socket.c in the Linux kernel’s SCTP subsystem. This flaw allows guests with local user privileges to trigger a deadlock and potentially crash the system.

A vulnerability was reported in the Open vSwitch sub-component in the Linux Kernel. The flaw occurs when a recursive operation of code push recursively calls into the code block. The OVS module does not validate the stack depth, pushing too many frames and causing a stack overflow. As a result, this can lead to a crash or other related issues.
A heap overflow flaw was found in 389-ds-base. This issue leads to a denial of service when writing a value larger than 256 chars in log_entry_attr.

An off-by-one error flaw was found in the udevListInterfacesByStatus() function in libvirt when the number of interfaces exceeds the size of the `names` array. This issue can be reproduced by sending specially crafted data to the libvirt daemon, allowing an unprivileged client to perform a denial of service attack by causing the libvirt daemon to crash.

A vulnerability was found in Undertow. This issue requires enabling the learning-push handler in the server's config, which is disabled by default, leaving the maxAge config in the handler unconfigured. The default is -1, which makes the handler vulnerable. If someone overwrites that config, the server is not subject to the attack. The attacker needs to be able to reach the server with a normal HTTP request.
A vulnerability was found in OpenJPEG similar to CVE-2019-6988. This flaw allows an attacker to bypass existing protections and cause an application crash through a maliciously crafted file.

A flaw was found in QEMU. An assertion failure was present in the usb_ep_get() function in hw/net/core.c when trying to get the USB endpoint from a USB device. This flaw may allow a malicious unprivileged guest user to crash the QEMU process on the host and cause a denial of service condition.

A log spoofing flaw was found in the Tuned package due to improper sanitization of some API arguments. This flaw allows an attacker to pass a controlled sequence of characters; newlines can be inserted into the log. Instead of the 'evil' the attacker could mimic a valid TuneD log line and trick the administrator. The quotes '' are usually used in TuneD logs citing raw user input, so there will always be the ' character ending the spoofed input, and the administrator can easily overlook this. This logged string is later used in logging and in the output of utilities, for example, `tuned-adm get_instances` or other third-party programs that use Tuned's D-Bus interface for such operations.

A flaw was found in npm-serialize-javascript. The vulnerability occurs because the serialize-javascript module does not properly sanitize certain inputs, such as regex or other JavaScript object types, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code. This code could be executed when deserialized by a web browser, causing Cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. This issue is critical in environments where serialized data is sent to web clients, potentially compromising the security of the website or web application using this package.

A flaw was found in the X server's request handling. Non-zero 'bytes to ignore' in a client's request can cause the server to skip processing another client's request, potentially leading to a denial of service.

A flaw was found in the Keycloak LDAP User Federation provider. This vulnerability allows an authenticated realm administrator to trigger deserialization of untrusted Java objects via a malicious LDAP server configuration.

A flaw was found in libssh. A remote attacker, by controlling client configuration files or known_hosts files, could craft specific hostnames that when processed by the `match_pattern()` function can lead to inefficient regular expression backtracking. This can cause timeouts and resource exhaustion, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for the client.

Multiple uses of uninitialized variables were found in libopensc that may lead to information disclosure or application crash. An attack requires a crafted USB device or smart card that would present the system with specially crafted responses to the APDUs

A vulnerability was found in kronosnet's (version <=1.34) cryptographic configuration management. The framework does not correctly zero-out or wipe sensitive memory segments after executing changes to its cryptographic configuration. This omission leaves raw encryption keys resident in memory after the associated structures are freed. A local attacker capable of leveraging memory disclosure techniques could exploit this flaw to retrieve the active encryption key, allowing them to decrypt cluster network communications or inject malicious packets to cause severe high-availability cluster instability.

BlueZ sdp-xml.c type confusion via RegisterProfile(ServiceRecord) can crash bluetoothd (local DoS): a crafted nested ServiceRecord can corrupt the SDP XML parser stack so scalar union data is treated as a sequence pointer, allowing a local caller to crash bluetoothd.

A flaw was found in the Seattle FilmWorks plugin in GIMP. When processing a specially crafted SFW image file, the plugin allocates a Variable-Length Array (VLA) on the stack without integer overflow checks, causing an unbounded stack allocation. This issue leads to an application crash, resulting in a denial of service.

A flaw was found in Flatpak. A Time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition exists in the `org.freedesktop.Flatpak.SystemHelper` component. This vulnerability occurs because a privileged `chmod` operation executes before the OSTree repository validation within the `Deploy()` function. An attacker can exploit this timing window to redirect symlinks to arbitrary files, potentially leading to unauthorized file manipulation or information disclosure.
A flaw was found in Podman. If an attacker can pass a crafted tar archive to the `podman load` command, they can create files on the host machine with the privileges of the user running Podman.

Flatpak's process ID namespace separation does not prevent a sandboxed app's kill(0, signal) or killpg(0, signal) calls from reaching processes outside the sandbox that share the same process group. A malicious or compromised Flatpak app can use this to cause denial of service by terminating processes outside its sandbox, such as the desktop shell.

A flaw was found in FreeType, specifically within its CID font loader. A remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking a user into opening content that embeds or references a specially crafted CID-keyed font. This crafted font can cause repeated allocations and decryptions of subroutine data across multiple font dictionaries, leading to excessive memory and CPU consumption. This can result in a denial of service (DoS) for the application or service processing the font, potentially causing it to hang or terminate.
Buffer over-read in Servicing Stack Updates allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

A flaw was found in evolution-data-server. Calendar events containing a file:// URI in their ATTACH property automatically read the targeted local file, base64-encode its contents and upload it back to the server when the event is saved. There are no file path restrictions or checks to verify whether the attachment originally came from the server or was added locally. This allows an attacker with access to a shared CalDAV calendar to exfiltrate arbitrary files the user has access to when interacting with malicious calendar events.

FFmpeg 8.1 through 9.0.2 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the libavcodec/exif.c parser that allows attackers to amplify allocations by pointing many IFD entries at overlapping payloads. Attackers can embed a small crafted EXIF block in TIFF, JPEG, PNG or WebP images to trigger quadratic memory allocation, causing denial of service in decoding applications.

FFmpeg through 9.0.2 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in pcm_dvd_encode_frame() in libavcodec/pcm-dvdenc.c when a 24-bit final frame holds fewer samples than one block. Attackers can supply 24-bit 48 or 96 kHz audio whose length leaves a short final frame, causing the loop counter to wrap and crash the transcoding process.
Out-of-bounds read in Windows Management Instrumentation allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.
Improper access control in Microsoft Account allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering locally.
Improper privilege management in Windows Deployment Services allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.
Weak authentication in Windows State Repository Service allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering locally.
Use of uninitialized resource in Windows Win32K allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.
Out-of-bounds read in Remote Desktop Client allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

Open Robotics ROS 2 sros2 load_policy XML External Entity Processing Information Disclosure Vulnerability. This vulnerability allows remote attackers to disclose sensitive information on affected installations of Open Robotics ROS 2. User interaction is required to exploit this vulnerability in that the target must visit a malicious page or open a malicious file.

The specific flaw exists within the parsing of policy XML files.
